title: Risk Factors of the Spread of COVID-19 in Prisoners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify and synthesize evidence on risk factors for COVID-19 in incarcerated populations. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar was conducted for English articles until October 2025. Study quality was assessed using the PRISMA checklist and NOS tool. Meta-analysis was performed in Stata 17 using a random-effects model, with odds ratios as the primary effect measure and statistical significance set at P < 0.05. Heterogeneity was evaluated via I2 statistics. RESULTS: Twelve articles were ultimately included in the study. For the meta-analysis, only 5 articles were considered, which evaluated sex, age, and vaccination status as the risk factors of COVID-19. The total sample size was 176169, consisting of 169117 males and 7,726 females. In most studies, the average age was reported to be around 40 years. Fully vaccinated prisoners were less likely to contract COVID-19 than unvaccinated ones (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.22, 0.67; P = 0.001), while no significant relationships were found regarding sex and age. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings confirm that full vaccination significantly protects against COVID-19 in prisons. Prioritizing vaccination campaigns, along with measures like mask use and hand hygiene, is essential to protect incarcerated individuals and the wider community.

title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
abstract: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In 70.2% of patients (33/47) with mAb-resistant SARS-CoV-2 infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the specific SARS-CoV-2 variants involved in the included cases, limiting the ability to assess variant-specific efficacy of CCP. Additionally, the small sample size (n=47) and inclusion of unpublished cases may introduce selection bias, and the lack of a control group precludes definitive causal inference.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize randomized controlled trials to validate the efficacy of CCP in immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection post-mAb failure, stratifying by variant type and CCP titre. Surveillance programs should monitor CCP efficacy against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants to guide clinical use.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes associated with improved outcomes. The review highlights CCP as a potential polyclonal alternative to mAbs in resistant infections, though small sample size, unpublished case inclusion, and variant-specific data gaps limit generalizability. Key priorities include randomized trials to confirm efficacy, variant-stratified analyses, and enhanced surveillance to track CCP performance against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In 70.2% of patients (33/47) with mAb-resistant SARS-CoV-2 infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the specific SARS-CoV-2 variants involved in the included cases, limiting the ability to assess variant-specific efficacy of CCP. Additionally, the small sample size (n=47) and inclusion of unpublished cases may introduce selection bias, and the lack of a control group precludes definitive causal inference.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize randomized controlled trials to validate the efficacy of CCP in immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection post-mAb failure, stratifying by variant type and CCP titre. Surveillance programs should monitor CCP efficacy against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants to guide clinical use.

title_zh: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
source_body_en: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.
abstract: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use. We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Thirty-one studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) were included. The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response. Among RCTs analysing timing, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration; for titre, 3 of 4 RCTs with explicit comparisons found benefit with higher-titre CP; and two large RCTs (combined n = 12,522) demonstrated preferential benefit in seronegative recipients. This interpretation is consistent with modelling estimates that CP, deployed largely to hospitalised patients, nonetheless saved tens of thousands of lives in the United States during the first pandemic year, an effect attributed to the subset treated early enough to modify disease progression. A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment. These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in treating COVID-19, focusing on three key determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics. The review includes 31 studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) and employs a design-stratified narrative synthesis approach. The findings emphasize the need for targeted use of CP and suggest a framework for its precision deployment in future pandemics.

title: Inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of critically ill COVID-19 patients is not associated with increased mortality: a systematic review with exploratory meta-analysis
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, inter-hospital transfer of critically ill patients between intensive care units was widely used to manage capacity shortages. While several individual studies have compared outcomes of transferred and non-transferred patients, no systematic synthesis of this evidence exists. This systematic review aims to determine whether inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of adult COVID-19 patients is associated with increased mortality or other adverse clinical outcomes. We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes of adult COVID-19 patients who underwent inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer with non-transferred ICU patients. Two reviewers screened, selected, and extracted data independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Exploratory random-effects meta-analyses were performed separately for each effect measure, with Hartung-Knapp and crude-effect sensitivity analyses. Nine observational studies from seven countries were included (approximately 6,100 transferred and 29,200 non-transferred ICU patients). None of the adjusted effect estimates showed a statistically significant mortality disadvantage for transferred patients. title: Allosteric effects of CDR-H3 mutations modulate binding and neutralization of a conserved SARS-CoV-2 RBD-targeting antibody
abstract: UNLABELLED: SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to erode the activity of first-generation monoclonal antibodies, underscoring the value of antibodies that recognize conserved features within the spike receptor-binding domain (RBD). As a model for breadth-oriented engineering, we assessed the RBD-directed antibody XG83, which has a CDRH3-dominated paratope. Utilizing the XG83-Wuhan RBD crystal structure as a reference, we integrated MOE alanine scanning and residue scanning with CDRH3 (A116-Y132) to identify chemically reasonable replacements and test interaction to an Omicron BA.1 RBD. The parental CDRH3-centric pose in comparative docking had a better score (-280.18) than the mutant MuXG83 (-254.2), along with 100-ns molecular dynamics showed that MuXG83 was less stable (with higher RMSD/RMSF with less favorable interaction energy). The ELISA results against Omicron BA.1 RBD demonstrated that XG83 had 40% stronger binding than MuXG83; convergence happened only at the highest concentration, concordant with SPR studies and the fact that mutation increased dissociation. According to this binding gap, BA.1 pseudovirus neutralization demonstrated that XG83 was much more powerful than MuXG83, showing that the E118L/F130H CDR-H3 alterations decreased functional activity against Omicron BA.1. These results imply that allosteric influences on interface stability and conformational dynamics by non-epitope CDR-H3 residues can affect antibody performance. Functional testing was confined to Omicron BA.1; therefore, larger variant-panel studies are needed to ascertain if such mutations affect antibody breadth. Our findings highlight a structure-guided approach for optimizing paratopes and indicate that non-epitope (potentially allosteric) changes to CDRH3 are also important while investigating potential development and neutralization before advancement. IMPORTANCE: This study shows how modest allosteric characteristics in CDR-H3 control the delicate balance between neutralizing potency and breadth, making a timely and significant addition to SARS-CoV-2 antibody engineering. Using crystallography, alanine scanning, residue scanning, docking, molecular dynamics, and experimental ELISA and neutralization assays, this study offers a structure-guided framework for rational paratope optimization. The discovery of CDR-H3 residues that regulate long-range stability rather than just direct epitope contacts reveals an unappreciated aspect of antibody design and explains why some alterations improve anticipated interactions but degrade functional performance. Importantly, the comparison of wild-type XG83 and modified MuXG83 shows how allosteric tuning affects antibody-antigen compatibility in developing variations like Omicron. These findings illuminate conserved RBD recognition and offer strategies for building next-generation therapeutic antibodies that are more resistant to viral evolution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution has reduced the efficacy of first-generation monoclonal antibodies, creating a need for antibodies that target conserved regions within the spike receptor-binding domain (RBD). The study aimed to model breadth-oriented antibody engineering by assessing the RBD-directed antibody XG83, which relies heavily on its CDRH3 paratope for binding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a structure-guided framework combining crystallography, alanine and residue scanning, docking, molecular dynamics, and experimental assays to compare the wild-type antibody XG83 with a modified variant, MuXG83, focusing on CDRH3 interactions with the Omicron BA.1 RBD.
analysis.methods: Crystallography provided the XG83-Wuhan RBD reference structure, while MOE-based alanine and residue scanning identified CDRH3 (A116-Y132) replacements. Docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics assessed stability and interaction energy, and ELISA, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and pseudovirus neutralization measured binding and functional activity against Omicron BA.1.
analysis.main_results: The parental XG83 showed a better docking score (-280.18 vs. -254.2) and greater stability in molecular dynamics, with lower RMSD/RMSF and more favorable interaction energy than MuXG83. ELISA and SPR revealed that XG83 had 40% stronger binding than MuXG83, and pseudovirus neutralization demonstrated that XG83 was significantly more potent against Omicron BA.1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that non-epitope CDRH3 residues exert allosteric effects on interface stability and conformational dynamics, thereby modulating antibody performance. They highlight that such allosteric tuning is an underappreciated aspect of antibody design, revealing how subtle changes can unexpectedly degrade functional activity despite improving predicted interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the engineering of next-generation therapeutic antibodies by demonstrating that allosteric modulation of CDRH3 can enhance resistance to viral evolution. This approach may guide the development of antibodies with broader neutralization capacity against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to functional testing against Omicron BA.1, leaving uncertainty about the breadth of effects across other variants. The evidence is moderate, as the conclusions are based on a single variant and rely on computational predictions validated by experimental assays, warranting further validation in broader variant panels.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how allosteric effects of CDRH3 mutations influence the binding and neutralization of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-targeting antibody XG83 against the Omicron BA.1 variant. Using a structure-guided framework, the authors compared the wild-type antibody with a modified variant, MuXG83, and found that the parental XG83 exhibited superior docking scores, stability, binding affinity, and neutralization potency. The findings reveal that non-epitope CDRH3 residues can exert allosteric control over antibody performance, challenging the assumption that direct epitope contacts alone determine functional outcomes. While the study provides valuable insights into antibody engineering, its conclusions are limited to Omicron BA.1, and broader variant testing is needed to confirm the generalizability of these effects.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗原性 进化 已降低首代单克隆抗体的有效性,亟需针对刺突蛋白受体结合域(RBD)内保守区域的抗体。本研究旨在通过评估高度依赖其 CDR-H3 抗原结合片段(paratope)进行结合的 RBD 导向抗体 XG83,对面向广谱性的抗体工程进行建模。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用结构引导框架,结合晶体学、丙氨酸和残基扫描、对接、分子动力学和实验测定,将野生型抗体 XG83 与修饰变体 MuXG83 进行比较,重点关注 CDRH3 与 Omicron BA.1 RBD 的相互作用。
elements_zh.methods: 晶体学提供了 XG83-Wuhan RBD 参考结构,而基于 MOE 的丙氨酸和残基扫描确定了 CDRH3 (A116-Y132) 替代品。对接和 100 纳秒分子动力学评估稳定性和相互作用能,ELISA、表面等离子共振 (SPR) 和假病毒中和测量针对 Omicron BA.1 的结合和功能活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 亲本 XG83 表现出更好的对接分数(-280.18 vs. -254.2)和更高的分子动力学稳定性,比 MuXG83 具有更低的 RMSD/RMSF 和更有利的相互作用能。ELISA 和 SPR 显示 XG83 的结合力比 MuXG83 强 40%,假病毒中和表明 XG83 对抗 Omicron BA.1 的效力明显更强。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,非表位 CDRH3 残基对界面稳定性和构象动力学发挥变构作用,从而调节抗体性能。他们强调,这种变构调整是抗体设计中一个未被充分认识的方面,揭示了尽管改善了预测的相互作用,但细微的变化如何会意外地降低功能活性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现证明 CDRH3 的变构调节可以增强对病毒 进化 的抵抗力,为下一代治疗抗体的工程设计提供了信息。这种方法可以指导针对新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体具有更广泛中和能力的抗体的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于针对 Omicron BA.1 的功能测试,因此对其他变体的影响广度存在不确定性。证据是温和的,因为结论是基于单个变体,并依赖于通过实验分析验证的计算预测,需要在更广泛的变体小组中进一步验证。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗原性 进化 已降低首代单克隆抗体的有效性,亟需针对刺突蛋白受体结合域(RBD)内保守区域的抗体。本研究旨在通过评估高度依赖其 CDR-H3 抗原结合片段(paratope)进行结合的 RBD 导向抗体 XG83,对面向广谱性的抗体工程进行建模。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用结构引导框架,结合晶体学、丙氨酸和残基扫描、对接、分子动力学和实验测定,将野生型抗体 XG83 与修饰变体 MuXG83 进行比较,重点关注 CDRH3 与 Omicron BA.1 RBD 的相互作用。
analysis_zh.methods: 晶体学提供了 XG83-Wuhan RBD 参考结构,而基于 MOE 的丙氨酸和残基扫描确定了 CDRH3 (A116-Y132) 替代品。对接和 100 纳秒分子动力学评估稳定性和相互作用能,ELISA、表面等离子共振 (SPR) 和假病毒中和测量针对 Omicron BA.1 的结合和功能活性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 亲本 XG83 表现出更好的对接分数(-280.18 vs. -254.2)和更高的分子动力学稳定性,比 MuXG83 具有更低的 RMSD/RMSF 和更有利的相互作用能。ELISA 和 SPR 显示 XG83 的结合力比 MuXG83 强 40%,假病毒中和表明 XG83 对抗 Omicron BA.1 的效力明显更强。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,非表位 CDRH3 残基对界面稳定性和构象动力学发挥变构作用,从而调节抗体性能。他们强调,这种变构调整是抗体设计中一个未被充分认识的方面,揭示了尽管改善了预测的相互作用,但细微的变化如何会意外地降低功能活性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现证明 CDRH3 的变构调节可以增强对病毒 进化 的抵抗力,为下一代治疗抗体的工程设计提供了信息。这种方法可以指导针对新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体具有更广泛中和能力的抗体的开发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于针对 Omicron BA.1 的功能测试,因此对其他变体的影响广度存在不确定性。证据是温和的,因为结论是基于单个变体,并依赖于通过实验分析验证的计算预测,需要在更广泛的变体小组中进一步验证。

title: Critical role of vaccination in preventing severe coronavirus disease 2019: perspectives from clinical outcomes in an Australian kidney transplant recipient cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) disproportionately experience severe COVID-19 infections. We previously identified concern regarding vaccine-induced rejection as a barrier to vaccine uptake. AIM: This study assesses COVID-19 vaccine uptake, infection outcomes and allograft rejection in KTRs during the delta and omicron waves (BA.1/BA.2). METHODS: This cohort study included all adult KTRs with a functioning allograft at 22 March 2021 at our centre. KTR and vaccination-related risk factors for the primary outcome of severe COVID-19 infection (requiring hospitalisation) and the secondary outcomes of death and all COVID-19 infections were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Rejection risk following infection/vaccination was also assessed. RESULTS: Of the 986 included KTRs, there were 333 (33.8%) COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) severe infections and 13 deaths (n = 13/333, 3.9%). Vaccine number was the most significant modifiable predictor of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio, per additional dose, 0.5; 95% confidence interval, 0.40-0.65, P < 0.001) and death. While older age also predicted severe infection and death, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate, history of diabetes and previous allograft rejection predicted severe infection. Male gender was the only predictor of all infections. Mycophenolate dose, prednisolone use and vaccine type did not predict infection or severe disease. Infections and vaccinations did not increase the risk of rejection. CONCLUSIONS: KTRs should be encouraged to be optimally vaccinated to prevent severe disease and can be reassured about the low risk of allograft rejection. Risk factors that compound the state of immunocompromise and severe COVID-19 infections should prompt vigilance and targeted interventions to mitigate these risks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) face disproportionately severe outcomes from COVID-19, and vaccine hesitancy due to concerns about allograft rejection may further increase risk. This study aimed to quantify COVID-19 vaccine uptake, infection outcomes, and rejection risk in KTRs during the Delta and Omicron waves.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted at a single centre, enrolling all adult KTRs with a functioning allograft as of 22 March 2021. The study period covered the Delta and Omicron (BA.1/BA.2) waves.
analysis.methods: Vaccination status and KTR-related risk factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models to determine predictors of severe COVID-19 infection (hospitalisation), death, and all infections. Rejection risk following infection or vaccination was also evaluated.
analysis.main_results: Among 986 KTRs, 333 (33.8%) had COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) were severe, and 13 deaths occurred (3.9%). Each additional vaccine dose reduced the risk of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001) and death. Older age, lower eGFR, diabetes, and prior allograft rejection predicted severe infection, while male gender predicted all infections. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not predict outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that higher vaccine uptake significantly reduces severe COVID-19 and mortality in KTRs without increasing rejection risk, addressing concerns about vaccine-induced allograft damage. This provides direct clinical evidence supporting optimal vaccination in this high-risk group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritising vaccination in KTRs to prevent severe disease and mortality, while reassuring clinicians and patients about the low risk of rejection. Targeted interventions for immunocompromised patients with compounding risk factors are warranted.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre design and lack of randomisation limit generalisability and causal inference. However, robust statistical adjustment and clear outcome definitions strengthen the evidence. The study provides moderate-strength evidence for vaccine efficacy in KTRs.

analysis.summary_en: This cohort study of 986 kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) assessed COVID-19 outcomes during the Delta and Omicron waves, focusing on vaccine uptake, severe infection, mortality, and allograft rejection. Vaccination was the strongest modifiable predictor of reduced severe disease and death, with each additional dose halving the risk (adjusted HR 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001). Older age, diabetes, lower kidney function, and prior rejection also increased severe infection risk, while male gender predicted any infection. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not influence outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk. The study concludes that KTRs should be optimally vaccinated to prevent severe COVID-19 and can be reassured about rejection risk. Limitations include a single-centre design and observational nature, but robust statistical methods support the findings.

analysis_en.methods: Vaccination status and KTR-related risk factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models to determine predictors of severe COVID-19 infection (hospitalisation), death, and all infections. Rejection risk following infection or vaccination was also evaluated.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 986 KTRs, 333 (33.8%) had COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) were severe, and 13 deaths occurred (3.9%). Each additional vaccine dose reduced the risk of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001) and death. Older age, lower eGFR, diabetes, and prior allograft rejection predicted severe infection, while male gender predicted all infections. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not predict outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that higher vaccine uptake significantly reduces severe COVID-19 and mortality in KTRs without increasing rejection risk, addressing concerns about vaccine-induced allograft damage. This provides direct clinical evidence supporting optimal vaccination in this high-risk group.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritising vaccination in KTRs to prevent severe disease and mortality, while reassuring clinicians and patients about the low risk of rejection. Targeted interventions for immunocompromised patients with compounding risk factors are warranted.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre design and lack of randomisation limit generalisability and causal inference. However, robust statistical adjustment and clear outcome definitions strengthen the evidence. The study provides moderate-strength evidence for vaccine efficacy in KTRs.

title_zh: 疫苗接种 在预防 2019 年严重冠状病毒病中的关键作用:澳大利亚肾移植受者 队列研究 临床结果的观点
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) disproportionately experience severe COVID-19 infections. We previously identified concern regarding vaccine-induced rejection as a barrier to vaccine uptake. AIM: This study assesses COVID-19 vaccine uptake, infection outcomes and allograft rejection in KTRs during the delta and omicron waves (BA.1/BA.2). METHODS: This cohort study included all adult KTRs with a functioning allograft at 22 March 2021 at our centre. KTR and vaccination-related risk factors for the primary outcome of severe COVID-19 infection (requiring hospitalisation) and the secondary outcomes of death and all COVID-19 infections were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Rejection risk following infection/vaccination was also assessed. RESULTS: Of the 986 included KTRs, there were 333 (33.8%) COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) severe infections and 13 deaths (n = 13/333, 3.9%). Vaccine number was the most significant modifiable predictor of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio, per additional dose, 0.5; 95% confidence interval, 0.40-0.65, P < 0.001) and death. While older age also predicted severe infection and death, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate, history of diabetes and previous allograft rejection predicted severe infection. Male gender was the only predictor of all infections. Mycophenolate dose, prednisolone use and vaccine type did not predict infection or severe disease. Infections and vaccinations did not increase the risk of rejection. CONCLUSIONS: KTRs should be encouraged to be optimally vaccinated to prevent severe disease and can be reassured about the low risk of allograft rejection. Risk factors that compound the state of immunocompromise and severe COVID-19 infections should prompt vigilance and targeted interventions to mitigate these risks.

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在 KTR 中优先考虑 疫苗接种 以预防严重疾病和 死亡率,同时让临床医生和患者放心排斥风险较低。对具有复合危险因素的免疫功能低下患者进行有针对性的干预是必要的。

title: Comparative immunogenicity of mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 SARS-CoV-2 bivalent booster vaccines in US nursing home residents.
abstract: Nursing home residents (NHRs) remain among the most vulnerable to severe outcomes from SARS-CoV-2 infection. While mRNA-1273 (Spikevax, Moderna) and BNT162b2 (Comirnaty, Pfizer-BioNTech) vaccines are widely used in this population, comparative data on their immunogenicity, particularly after bivalent boosters, remain limited. We conducted a longitudinal immunologic evaluation of U.S. NHRs who received either the mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 bivalent vaccine. Serum samples were collected 10-30 d post-vaccination. Anti-spike IgG levels were measured using a Luminex bead-based assay, and neutralizing titers were assessed via pseudovirus neutralization. Comparative analyses of the titer distributions were performed using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Both vaccine groups demonstrated strong humoral responses to the ancestral Wuhan strain and Omicron BA.4/5 subvariants. Spike-binding antibody levels and neutralization titers were comparable between the mRNA -1273 and BNT162b2 vaccine formulations. Conclusions: Both mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 mRNA vaccines elicit similarly robust humoral immunity in NHRs, supporting their interchangeable use in booster strategies. Our findings underscore the importance of timely booster administration over exact product selection in protecting this high-risk, immunosenescent population.

title: Plasma concentrations of nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir required for inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 replication differ between rhesus macaques and humans
abstract: ABSTRACT Early during the COVID-19 pandemic, non-human primate (NHP) infection models emerged as highly useful tools for preclinical screening of antiviral drugs. However, it is uncertain whether NHP models can be used to precisely inform optimal dosing in humans. We previously established and validated mathematical models, which were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials. These models identified that plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans ( in vivo EC50) differ substantially from in vitro EC50 estimates in cell culture systems. Here, we apply models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. We identify that equivalent plasma drug concentrations correspond to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RM (30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs) was estimated to be less than in humans (82%) due to shorter plasma drug half-life. Molnupiravir efficacy in RMs (95% in nasal and 99% in the lungs) is estimated to be similar to efficacy in humans against omicron variants. Our model estimates that 10-fold higher plasma nirmatelvir concentrations are needed in humans versus RMs to achieve 50% reduction in viral replication, whereas 20-fold lower plasma molnupiravir concentrations are needed. Our results suggest that dose optimization in humans based on modeling of NHP viral loads is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles, and that data from human phase 1 and 2 trials are better suited for this task.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether non-human primate (NHP) infection models can precisely inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs in humans during the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlighted uncertainty in translating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing requirements for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study applied mathematical models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were either untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. The models were previously established and validated using SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials.
analysis.methods: Mathematical models were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials to estimate plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans. These models were then applied to viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques to estimate antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations.
analysis.main_results: Equivalent plasma drug concentrations corresponded to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for both nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RMs was estimated at 30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs, lower than the 82% efficacy estimated in humans due to a shorter plasma drug half-life.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that dose optimization in humans based on NHP viral load modeling is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. They concluded that human phase 1 and 2 trial data are better suited for determining optimal dosing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against directly extrapolating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing, emphasizing the need for human trial data to inform drug dosing strategies for SARS-CoV-2. This has implications for the design of preclinical studies and the translation of antiviral efficacy from animal models to clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that dose optimization in humans based on NHP modeling is constrained by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on modeling and the limited generalizability of NHP data to humans.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated whether non-human primate (NHP) models can accurately inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs for SARS-CoV-2 in humans. Using mathematical models previously validated with human clinical trial data, the authors analyzed viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both. They found that antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations differed between NHP and humans, with nirmatrelvir showing lower efficacy in RMs (30–46%) than in humans (82%) due to shorter drug half-life. Molnupiravir efficacy was similar between RMs and humans. The authors concluded that NHP-derived antiviral efficacy cannot be directly translated to human dosing and that human phase 1–2 trial data are essential for dose optimization.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether non-human primate (NHP) infection models can precisely inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs in humans during the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlighted uncertainty in translating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing requirements for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study applied mathematical models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were either untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. The models were previously established and validated using SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials.
analysis_en.methods: Mathematical models were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials to estimate plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans. These models were then applied to viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques to estimate antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations.
analysis_en.main_results: Equivalent plasma drug concentrations corresponded to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for both nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RMs was estimated at 30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs, lower than the 82% efficacy estimated in humans due to a shorter plasma drug half-life.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that dose optimization in humans based on NHP viral load modeling is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. They concluded that human phase 1 and 2 trial data are better suited for determining optimal dosing.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against directly extrapolating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing, emphasizing the need for human trial data to inform drug dosing strategies for SARS-CoV-2. This has implications for the design of preclinical studies and the translation of antiviral efficacy from animal models to clinical practice.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that dose optimization in humans based on NHP modeling is constrained by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on modeling and the limited generalizability of NHP data to humans.

title_zh: 恒河猴和人类抑制 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 复制所需的 nirmatrelvir 和 molnupiravir 血浆浓度不同
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Early during the COVID-19 pandemic, non-human primate (NHP) infection models emerged as highly useful tools for preclinical screening of antiviral drugs. However, it is uncertain whether NHP models can be used to precisely inform optimal dosing in humans. We previously established and validated mathematical models, which were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials. These models identified that plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans ( in vivo EC50) differ substantially from in vitro EC50 estimates in cell culture systems. Here, we apply models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. We identify that equivalent plasma drug concentrations correspond to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RM (30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs) was estimated to be less than in humans (82%) due to shorter plasma drug half-life. Molnupiravir efficacy in RMs (95% in nasal and 99% in the lungs) is estimated to be similar to efficacy in humans against omicron variants. Our model estimates that 10-fold higher plasma nirmatelvir concentrations are needed in humans versus RMs to achieve 50% reduction in viral replication, whereas 20-fold lower plasma molnupiravir concentrations are needed. Our results suggest that dose optimization in humans based on modeling of NHP viral loads is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles, and that data from human phase 1 and 2 trials are better suited for this task.

title: The impact of expanded adolescent vaccination against COVID-19 depends on the epidemic status: a mathematical modelling study
abstract: Abstract Background/ObjectivesWe evaluated the impact of the COVID-19 adolescent vaccination in England at two different epidemic points: the autumn (August-November) 2021, in the presence of a large Omicron epidemic wave, and the autumn (August-November) 2022, when the subsequent Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage. MethodsUsing the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England, under varying vaccine uptake and onset time, we evaluated the impact of a)vaccinating 18+ only versus additional 12+ vaccination from the autumn 2021; and b)the current immunisation strategy at the time versus additional 12+ vaccination from September 2022, projecting the number of new daily SARS-CoV-2 infections, hospitalisations and deaths. ResultsIn presence of the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, the expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all-ages, 1,010,000 SARS-CoV-2 infections in the period 2-6 months from vaccine onset in the vaccinated cohort. During the Omicron waves in 2022, additional adolescents vaccination did not significantly reduce the COVID-19 burden in the entire population, nor within the vaccinated cohort. ConclusionsOur findings highlight that adolescent vaccination impact depends on the timing/speed of implementation, other present intervention strategies, and the status of the epidemic at the time and it should not be considered as a stand-alone immunisation strategy. HighlightsO_LIFirst study to compare the impact of expanding adolescent COVID-19 vaccination at two different epidemic points: one when a large epidemic is spreading and another at a more endemic stage of the epidemic. C_LIO_LIEarlier implementation at sufficient coverage was more effective in reducing the number of infections at the peak of the Omicron wave, and getting ahead of the epidemic spread. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, adolescent vaccination was not necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. MethodsUsing the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England, under varying vaccine uptake and onset time, we evaluated the impact of a)vaccinating 18+ only versus additional 12+ vaccination from the autumn 2021; and b)the current immunisation strategy at the time versus additional 12+ vaccination from September 2022, projecting the number of new daily SARS-CoV-2 infections, hospitalisations and deaths. ResultsIn presence of the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, the expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all-ages, 1,010,000 SARS-CoV-2 infections in the period 2-6 months from vaccine onset in the vaccinated cohort. During the Omicron waves in 2022, additional adolescents vaccination did not significantly reduce the COVID-19 burden in the entire population, nor within the vaccinated cohort. ConclusionsOur findings highlight that adolescent vaccination impact depends on the timing/speed of implementation, other present intervention strategies, and the status of the epidemic at the time and it should not be considered as a stand-alone immunisation strategy. HighlightsO_LIFirst study to compare the impact of expanding adolescent COVID-19 vaccination at two different epidemic points: one when a large epidemic is spreading and another at a more endemic stage of the epidemic. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2021, in the presence of the newly emerging Omicron variant, adolescent vaccination was necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. C_LIO_LIEarlier implementation at sufficient coverage was more effective in reducing the number of infections at the peak of the Omicron wave, and getting ahead of the epidemic spread. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, adolescent vaccination was not necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. C_LIO_LIOur work shows that implementation, timing and speed of an adolescent immunisation programmes should be considered in conjunction with the epidemic status, incidence and prevalence of the epidemic at that time.

title_original: The impact of expanded adolescent vaccination against COVID-19 depends on the epidemic status: a mathematical modelling study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how the impact of adolescent vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 varies depending on the epidemic status, specifically during the Omicron wave in late 2021 and its endemic phase in 2022.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mathematical modelling study using the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England assessed the impact of vaccinating 18+ only versus expanding to 12+ adolescents during two different epidemic periods: late 2021 with a large Omicron wave and 2022 when the epidemic was at an endemic stage.
analysis.methods: The study used the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model to simulate the effects of varying vaccine uptake and onset times, projecting the number of new daily infections, hospitalisations, and deaths under different vaccination strategies.
analysis.main_results: During the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all ages and 1,010,000 infections in the vaccinated cohort within 2-6 months. In 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, additional adolescent vaccination did not significantly reduce the overall burden of COVID-19 or within the vaccinated cohort.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the effectiveness of adolescent vaccination depends on the timing and speed of implementation, alongside other interventions and the epidemic status, and emphasized that it should not be considered as a standalone strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that public health strategies for adolescent vaccination should be tailored to the current epidemic status, incidence, and prevalence, ensuring optimal impact during periods of high transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on mathematical modelling, which may not fully capture real-world complexities, and the results are specific to England's context, limiting generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the impact of adolescent vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 during two distinct epidemic phases: the Omicron wave in late 2021 and its endemic stage in 2022. Using the Covasim model, it compares vaccinating 18+ only versus expanding to 12+ adolescents. Results show that expanded vaccination significantly reduced infections during the 2021 wave but had little effect in 2022 when the epidemic was endemic. The authors conclude that adolescent vaccination effectiveness depends on implementation timing and epidemic status, and it should not be used as a standalone strategy. The study highlights the importance of aligning vaccination programs with current epidemic dynamics. However, the findings are based on mathematical models and are specific to England, limiting their generalisability and evidence strength.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 Covasim 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 模型来模拟不同 疫苗 摄取和发病时间的影响,预测不同 疫苗 策略下每日新感染、住院和死亡的数量。
elements_zh.main_results: During the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all ages and 1,010,000 infections in the vaccinated cohort within 2-6 months. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,青少年 疫苗接种 的有效性取决于实施的时机和速度,以及其他干预措施和流行状况,并强调不应将其视为独立策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对青少年 疫苗接种 的公共卫生策略应根据当前的流行状况、发病率 和 患病率 进行调整,确保在高 传播 期间产生最佳影响。

title: Health-related quality of life among patients with long COVID according to the presence of a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long COVID is associated with poor health-related quality of life (QoL), with substantial interindividual variations. This study aimed to investigate the association between QoL and a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) among patients seeking care for long COVID. METHODS: Data were drawn from the CASPer-COVID program, a multidisciplinary tertiary care program for patients with persistent symptoms following COVID-19. QoL was evaluated with the 36-Item Short-Form health survey (SF-36), yielding a Physical Component Summary (PCS) and a Mental Component Summary (MCS). Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to investigate the associations between PCS or MCS scores and a diagnosis of FSD, adjusting for age, gender, body mass index, comorbidities, hospitalization for acute COVID-19, core persistent symptoms, symptom duration, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and physical activity. RESULTS: The analyses included 773 patients (median age [interquartile range (IQR)]: 44 [36-55] years; 64% women). QoL was markedly impaired (median PCS [IQR]: 44 [31-60]; median MCS [IQR]: 39 [31-49]). A diagnosis of FSD (76.5% of patients) was not associated with MCS (β [95% CI]: 1.11 [-1.30, 3.53]) or PCS (β [95% CI]: -1.60 [-3.88, 0.67]) scores in adjusted analyses. Lower PCS and MCS scores were associated with higher depressive and anxiety symptoms, lower physical activity levels, and pain. In addition, lower PCS scores were associated with female gender, hospitalization for acute COVID-19 and longer symptom duration. CONCLUSION: In patients seeking care for long COVID in a tertiary care setting, QoL did not differ significantly between those diagnosed with FSD and other patients.

title_original: Health-related quality of life among patients with long COVID according to the presence of a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder: A cross-sectional study.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines the association between health-related quality of life (QoL) and a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) among patients with long COVID, focusing on the SARS-CoV-2-related condition post-COVID condition (long COVID). The central question is whether FSD diagnosis correlates with impaired physical (PCS) or mental (MCS) component summary scores of QoL in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence is derived from a cross-sectional analysis within the CASPer-COVID program, a multidisciplinary tertiary care initiative for patients with persistent symptoms following COVID-19. QoL was measured using the SF-36 instrument, generating PCS and MCS scores. Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and psychological covariates to assess associations between QoL and FSD diagnosis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 773 patients with long COVID, QoL was markedly impaired, with median PCS and MCS scores of 44 and 39, respectively. No significant association was found between FSD diagnosis and either PCS (β [95% CI]: -1.60 [-3.88, 0.67]) or MCS (β [95% CI]: 1.11 [-1.30, 3.53]) scores after adjustment for confounders.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not evaluate the temporal dynamics of QoL changes or the impact of FSD diagnosis over time. Additionally, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the relationship between FSD and QoL in long COVID. analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study within the CASPer-COVID program assessed health-related quality of life (QoL) in 773 patients with long COVID, using SF-36 to derive Physical (PCS) and Mental (MCS) Component Summary scores. QoL was significantly impaired, with median PCS and MCS scores of 44 and 39, respectively. After adjusting for age, gender, comorbidities, hospitalization, symptom duration, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and physical activity, a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) was not associated with differences in PCS or MCS scores. The findings highlight the need for longitudinal research to explore causal pathways and inform targeted interventions for QoL improvement in long COVID.

title_zh: 根据功能性躯体疾病 诊断 的存在,长新冠 患者的健康相关生活质量:一项横断面研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Long COVID is associated with poor health-related quality of life (QoL), with substantial interindividual variations. This study aimed to investigate the association between QoL and a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) among patients seeking care for long COVID. METHODS: Data were drawn from the CASPer-COVID program, a multidisciplinary tertiary care program for patients with persistent symptoms following COVID-19. QoL was evaluated with the 36-Item Short-Form health survey (SF-36), yielding a Physical Component Summary (PCS) and a Mental Component Summary (MCS). Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to investigate the associations between PCS or MCS scores and a diagnosis of FSD, adjusting for age, gender, body mass index, comorbidities, hospitalization for acute COVID-19, core persistent symptoms, symptom duration, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and physical activity. RESULTS: The analyses included 773 patients (median age [interquartile range (IQR)]: 44 [36-55] years; 64% women). QoL was markedly impaired (median PCS [IQR]: 44 [31-60]; median MCS [IQR]: 39 [31-49]). A diagnosis of FSD (76.5% of patients) was not associated with MCS (β [95% CI]: 1.11 [-1.30, 3.53]) or PCS (β [95% CI]: -1.60 [-3.88, 0.67]) scores in adjusted analyses. Lower PCS and MCS scores were associated with higher depressive and anxiety symptoms, lower physical activity levels, and pain. In addition, lower PCS scores were associated with female gender, hospitalization for acute COVID-19 and longer symptom duration. CONCLUSION: In patients seeking care for long COVID in a tertiary care setting, QoL did not differ significantly between those diagnosed with FSD and other patients.

title: A structural and mechanistic atlas of NTD antibody neutralization and immune escape across SARS-CoV-2 prototype and its (sub-)variants.
abstract: The N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) is a critical antibody target, yet its epitope organization, neutralization mechanisms, and immune evasion strategies remain incompletely resolved. Here, we classify NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes (designated as NTD-1 to NTD-9), including a cryptic epitope defined here (NTD-8). Mechanistic studies reveal that NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, thereby extending this mechanism to selected NTD-directed antibodies. Format profiling shows that while most NTD antibodies require bivalency, selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain neutralizing activity in Fab form. Profiling 41 antibodies across prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants defines an epitope-resolved escape landscape and enables dissection of three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. Notably, the KP.3.1.1 subvariant uses a dual escape mechanism in which ∆S31 introduces N30 glycosylation and substantially remodels the S27-R34 region, undermining recognition by both NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies. These findings provide a structural and mechanistic framework for rational vaccine and antibody design resilient to antigenic drift.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title_original: A structural and mechanistic atlas of NTD antibody neutralization and immune escape across SARS-CoV-2 prototype and its (sub-)variants.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the incomplete understanding of how antibodies targeting the N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein neutralize the virus and how immune escape occurs across variants. It asks whether the epitope organization and neutralization mechanisms of NTD antibodies can be systematically classified and mechanistically explained to inform vaccine and antibody design.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research classifies NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across the SARS-CoV-2 prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. It includes mechanistic studies to dissect neutralization and escape strategies.
analysis.methods: Antibody classes were defined by spatial epitope mapping, and neutralization mechanisms were investigated through structural and functional assays. Escape landscapes were profiled by assessing antibody recognition across variants, including the KP.3.1.1 subvariant.
analysis.main_results: Nine NTD antibody classes (NTD-1 to NTD-9) were identified, including a cryptic epitope (NTD-8). NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, and selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant employs dual escape via ∆S31 introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, undermining NTD-5 and NTD-9 recognition.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work provides an epitope-resolved escape landscape and reveals three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. It introduces a structural and mechanistic framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can guide the development of next-generation vaccines and monoclonal antibodies with improved resilience to SARS-CoV-2 immune escape, particularly against Omicron subvariants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to structural and functional profiling in vitro and does not address in vivo efficacy, clinical outcomes, or population-level immune responses. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only scope and lack of direct clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study classifies SARS-CoV-2 N-terminal domain (NTD) antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. Mechanistic analyses reveal that NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, while selected antibodies retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant escapes neutralization via dual mechanisms: introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, disrupting recognition by NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies. The work defines an epitope-resolved escape landscape and identifies three convergent evasion strategies—contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling—providing a structural framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the incomplete understanding of how antibodies targeting the N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein neutralize the virus and how immune escape occurs across variants. It asks whether the epitope organization and neutralization mechanisms of NTD antibodies can be systematically classified and mechanistically explained to inform vaccine and antibody design.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The research classifies NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across the SARS-CoV-2 prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. It includes mechanistic studies to dissect neutralization and escape strategies.
elements_en.methods: Antibody classes were defined by spatial epitope mapping, and neutralization mechanisms were investigated through structural and functional assays. Escape landscapes were profiled by assessing antibody recognition across variants, including the KP.3.1.1 subvariant.
elements_en.main_results: Nine NTD antibody classes (NTD-1 to NTD-9) were identified, including a cryptic epitope (NTD-8). NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, and selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant employs dual escape via ∆S31 introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, undermining NTD-5 and NTD-9 recognition.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The work provides an epitope-resolved escape landscape and reveals three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. It introduces a structural and mechanistic framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can guide the development of next-generation vaccines and monoclonal antibodies with improved resilience to SARS-CoV-2 immune escape, particularly against Omicron subvariants.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to structural and functional profiling in vitro and does not address in vivo efficacy, clinical outcomes, or population-level immune responses. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only scope and lack of direct clinical validation.

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 原型及其(子)变体的 NTD 抗体中和和免疫逃逸的结构和机制图谱。
source_body_en: The N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) is a critical antibody target, yet its epitope organization, neutralization mechanisms, and immune evasion strategies remain incompletely resolved. Here, we classify NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes (designated as NTD-1 to NTD-9), including a cryptic epitope defined here (NTD-8). Mechanistic studies reveal that NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, thereby extending this mechanism to selected NTD-directed antibodies. Format profiling shows that while most NTD antibodies require bivalency, selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain neutralizing activity in Fab form. Profiling 41 antibodies across prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants defines an epitope-resolved escape landscape and enables dissection of three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. Notably, the KP.3.1.1 subvariant uses a dual escape mechanism in which ∆S31 introduces N30 glycosylation and substantially remodels the S27-R34 region, undermining recognition by both NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies. These findings provide a structural and mechanistic framework for rational vaccine and antibody design resilient to antigenic drift.
abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突 (S) 的 N 端结构域 (NTD) 是一个关键的抗体靶点,但其表位组织、中和机制和免疫逃避策略仍未完全解决。在这里,我们将 NTD 抗体分为九个空间不同的类别(指定为 NTD-1 至 NTD-9),包括此处定义的神秘表位 (NTD-8)。机制研究表明,NTD-5 和 NTD-9 抗体通过诱导 S1 脱落来中和,从而将该机制扩展到选定的 NTD 定向抗体。格式分析显示,虽然大多数 NTD 抗体需要二价,但来自 NTD-3、NTD-5 和 NTD-9 的选定抗体保留了 Fab 形式的中和活性。对原型、Delta 和 17 个 Omicron 亚变体的 41 种抗体进行分析,定义了表位解析的逃逸景观,并能够剖析三种聚合逃逸策略:接触残基破坏、聚糖屏蔽和构象重塑。值得注意的是,KP.3.1.1 亚变体使用双重逃逸机制,其中 ΔS31 引入 N30 糖基化并显着重塑 S27-R34 区域,从而破坏 NTD-5 和 NTD-9 抗体的识别。这些发现为合理的 疫苗 和抗抗原漂移的抗体设计提供了结构和机制框架。

title: Persistent humoral, cellular, and transcriptional signatures associated with protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 observed 18-months after COVID-19 vaccinations during the Omicron wave in Pakistan
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic the population experienced waves of SARS-CoV-2 infections as well as vaccinations. Concern with longer term effectiveness of vaccinations led to booster vaccinations across global population, more high resource settings but not in low middle income countries such as Pakistan. We studied a population which received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA and vector types) and were tested this one year and a half afterwards. Humoral responses determined through IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity studied through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens all indicated persistent protection against the coronavirus. Through a comparison with a pre-pandemic cohort, host blood transcriptional profiles of the post-vaccination cohort showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways reflective of vaccine associated changes. Additionally, cellular stress associated responses were apparent which are consistent with viral infection signatures as well as vaccination effects. Our results reflect an effect likely as a combination of COVID-19 vaccination and immune boosting due to SARS-CoV-2 transmission leading to trained immunity in the absence of COVID-19 boosters. It’s the first work of its kind- very limited information globally on post-pandemic immunity. It shows at the transcriptional level how immune activation is maintained, stress pathways and cellular senescence. These data show hybrid immunity likely gave longer-term protection observed in Pakistan despite limited COVID-19 vaccination availability, with relatively low morbidity and mortality.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed concerns about the durability of vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan where booster availability was limited during the Omicron wave.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research examined a population in Pakistan that had received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA, and vector types) and evaluated immune responses approximately 18 months after vaccination.
analysis.methods: The study assessed humoral immunity via IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens, alongside host blood transcriptional profiling to identify pathway changes associated with vaccine responses.
analysis.main_results: Humoral and cellular immune responses indicated persistent protection against SARS-CoV-2, and transcriptional profiles showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways consistent with vaccine-associated changes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that hybrid immunity—combining vaccination and natural infection—likely contributed to sustained protection in Pakistan despite limited booster availability, and noted this was among the first studies to characterize post-pandemic immunity at the transcriptional level.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that hybrid immunity may have provided longer-term protection in low-resource settings, potentially informing vaccination strategies and surveillance approaches in similar contexts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks detailed methodological, demographic, or statistical reporting, which constrains the strength of the conclusions and generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the durability of vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2 in a Pakistani population 18 months after receiving different COVID-19 vaccines during the Omicron wave. Using humoral, cellular, and transcriptional profiling, the authors observed persistent immune responses and upregulated cellular pathways indicative of vaccine-associated changes. They interpreted these findings as evidence that hybrid immunity—from vaccination and natural infection—likely sustained protection despite limited booster availability. The work is notable for being among the first to characterize post-pandemic immunity at the transcriptional level. However, the evidence is restricted to abstract-level data, limiting the strength and generalizability of the conclusions.

elements_zh.main_results: 体液和细胞 免疫应答 表明对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 具有持续的保护作用,转录谱显示细胞信号传导和蛋白质合成途径上调,与 疫苗 相关的变化一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明混合免疫(疫苗接种 和自然感染相结合)可能有助于巴基斯坦的持续保护,尽管加强剂的可用性有限,并指出这是首批在转录水平上表征大流行后免疫的研究之一。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于抽象级别的数据,缺乏详细的方法论、人口统计或统计报告,这限制了结论的强度和普遍性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed concerns about the durability of vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan where booster availability was limited during the Omicron wave.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The research examined a population in Pakistan that had received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA, and vector types) and evaluated immune responses approximately 18 months after vaccination.
analysis_en.methods: The study assessed humoral immunity via IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens, alongside host blood transcriptional profiling to identify pathway changes associated with vaccine responses.
analysis_en.main_results: Humoral and cellular immune responses indicated persistent protection against SARS-CoV-2, and transcriptional profiles showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways consistent with vaccine-associated changes.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that hybrid immunity—combining vaccination and natural infection—likely contributed to sustained protection in Pakistan despite limited booster availability, and noted this was among the first studies to characterize post-pandemic immunity at the transcriptional level.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that hybrid immunity may have provided longer-term protection in low-resource settings, potentially informing vaccination strategies and surveillance approaches in similar contexts.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks detailed methodological, demographic, or statistical reporting, which constrains the strength of the conclusions and generalizability.

title_zh: Persistent humoral, cellular, and transcriptional signatures associated with protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 observed 18-months after COVID-19 vaccinations during the Omicron wave in Pakistan
source_body_en: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic the population experienced waves of SARS-CoV-2 infections as well as vaccinations. Concern with longer term effectiveness of vaccinations led to booster vaccinations across global population, more high resource settings but not in low middle income countries such as Pakistan. We studied a population which received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA and vector types) and were tested this one year and a half afterwards. Humoral responses determined through IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity studied through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens all indicated persistent protection against the coronavirus. Through a comparison with a pre-pandemic cohort, host blood transcriptional profiles of the post-vaccination cohort showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways reflective of vaccine associated changes. Additionally, cellular stress associated responses were apparent which are consistent with viral infection signatures as well as vaccination effects. Our results reflect an effect likely as a combination of COVID-19 vaccination and immune boosting due to SARS-CoV-2 transmission leading to trained immunity in the absence of COVID-19 boosters. It’s the first work of its kind- very limited information globally on post-pandemic immunity. It shows at the transcriptional level how immune activation is maintained, stress pathways and cellular senescence. These data show hybrid immunity likely gave longer-term protection observed in Pakistan despite limited COVID-19 vaccination availability, with relatively low morbidity and mortality.

title: Epidemiology and mortality among hospital-acquired cases of COVID-19 in the pre-Omicron and Omicron periods: A data-linkage study in Victoria, Australia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to compare the epidemiology and mortality of hospital-acquired versus non-hospital-acquired COVID-19 infections among hospitalised patients. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of COVID‐19 hospitalisations in Victoria, Australia (January 2021-June 2024), using linked state surveillance systems. Episodes were classified as hospital acquired if the first positive test occurred ≥8 days post admission. Age, sex, intensive care unit admission and 30‐day mortality were compared between hospital-acquired and non‐hospital-acquired cases across pre‐Omicron and Omicron periods. RESULTS: Of 6,485 hospital-acquired and 62,670 non-hospital-acquired episodes, median age for hospital-acquired versus non-hospital-acquired cases was 77.8 versus 77.6 years before Omicron and 52.6 versus 73.1 years during Omicron. Monthly proportion of hospital-acquired cases increased during Omicron (range: 1% to 21%). Case fatality rates were higher in hospital-acquired than in non-hospital-acquired cases, with a larger difference before the Omicron (incidence rate ratio: 4.49, 95% confidence interval: 2.02, 9.99) than during the Omicron period (incidence rate ratio: 1.62, 95% confidence interval: 1.44, 1.82). Intensive care unit admission was associated with 30-day mortality for hospital-acquired (adjusted odds ratio: 4.4, 95% confidence interval: 2.3-8.4) and non‐hospital-acquired cases (adjusted odds ratio: 4.0, 95% confidence interval: 3.5-4.7). CONCLUSIONS: Hospital-acquired COVID-19 infections remain significant, associated with higher mortality rates than non-hospital-acquired infection and disproportionately affecting older patients. IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH: Our findings underscore the need for robust hospital COVID-19 infection prevention strategies.
journal: Australian and New Zealand journal of public health

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study in Victoria, Australia, compared hospital-acquired versus non-hospital-acquired COVID-19 across pre-Omicron and Omicron periods using linked surveillance data. Hospital-acquired cases were defined by a positive test at least eight days after admission. Among 6,485 hospital-acquired and 62,670 non-hospital-acquired episodes, median age was similar before Omicron but younger during Omicron for hospital-acquired cases. Monthly hospital-acquired cases rose to 21% under Omicron, and case fatality rates were higher for hospital-acquired cases, with incidence rate ratios of 4.49 pre-Omicron and 1.62 during Omicron. The authors conclude that hospital-acquired COVID-19 remains significant, disproportionately affecting older patients and carrying higher mortality than non-hospital-acquired infection. These findings support strengthening hospital infection prevention strategies.

title: Pathogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1 in immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaques.
abstract: Since the emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant, decreased morbidity and mortality relative to early strains have been widely reported. However, the virological characteristics of recent subvariants dominating the post-pandemic era remain to be fully elucidated. In the present study, the intrinsic pathogenicities of the Omicron subvariants JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1 were investigated using an immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaque model. All three variants exhibited robust replication in the upper respiratory tract, surpassing the viral titers observed with the early Wuhan strain. Omicron subvariant infection caused prolonged fever and sustained viral shedding in the nasal mucosa for at least seven days, indicating enhanced adaptation to upper airway tissues. Despite this shift in viral replication tropism, histological analysis showed that these variants retained the characteristics to induce lower respiratory tract disease. All infected macaques developed bronchopneumonia characterized by cellular exudates in the alveolar spaces. The histological scores were comparable to those observed with the early strain. These findings demonstrate that the pathogenicity of the Omicron subvariants has not been fully attenuated in the absence of pre-existing immunity, since they caused severe lung disease in immunologically naïve macaques. Furthermore, their enhanced propagation in the upper airway likely facilitates efficient transmission among humans. The continuous circulation of SARS-CoV-2 variants underscores the necessity of ongoing surveillance of viral gene variations and the maintenance of protective immunity in vulnerable populations.
