analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the incomplete understanding of the virological characteristics of recent SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants (JN.1, EG.5.1, BA.2.86.1) that emerged after the initial pandemic waves, despite reports of reduced morbidity and mortality compared to early strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research used an immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaque model to investigate the intrinsic pathogenicity of three Omicron subvariants: JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1.
analysis.methods: The study assessed viral replication, clinical signs, viral shedding, and histological lung damage in macaques experimentally infected with the specified Omicron subvariants.
analysis.main_results: All three Omicron subvariants replicated robustly in the upper respiratory tract, with viral titers exceeding those of the early Wuhan strain, and caused prolonged fever and sustained nasal viral shedding for at least seven days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that Omicron subvariants have not fully attenuated in pathogenicity in the absence of pre-existing immunity, as they induced severe bronchopneumonia in macaques, and their enhanced upper airway replication suggests potential for efficient human transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for continuous surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 genetic variations and the maintenance of protective immunity in vulnerable populations due to the ongoing circulation of variants with retained pathogenic potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to an immunologically naïve non-human primate model, which may not fully recapitulate human immune responses or disease severity, and the evidence strength is moderate given the absence of human clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the pathogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1 in immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaques to address gaps in understanding their virological characteristics post-pandemic. Using an experimental infection model, the authors observed robust upper respiratory tract replication, prolonged fever, and sustained nasal viral shedding exceeding levels seen with the early Wuhan strain. Despite this shift in tropism, all subvariants induced severe bronchopneumonia in the lower respiratory tract, with histological damage comparable to the early strain. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that Omicron subvariants have not fully attenuated in pathogenicity in the absence of pre-existing immunity and may retain efficient transmission potential due to enhanced upper airway replication. The study underscores the importance of ongoing genomic surveillance and maintaining protective immunity in vulnerable populations to mitigate the impact of circulating variants.

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2遗传变异的持续监测的必要性,以及由于具有保留致病潜力的变异体的持续循环而维持易感人群的保护性免疫力的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于免疫学上幼稚的非人类灵长类动物模型,该模型可能无法完全概括人类 免疫应答 或疾病严重程度,并且鉴于缺乏人类临床数据,证据强度中等。

title: Clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review and meta-analysis of global data.
abstract: Background COVID-19 pandemic has substantially affected neurosurgical care globally through service reorganizations, delayed presentation, alterations in case selection, and limited perioperative resources. However, overall impact of these changes on clinical outcomes in neurosurgical patients remains unclear. Hence, this review evaluated clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients managed during COVID-19 era compared with pre-pandemic era. Methods Systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science was conducted from inception of database till March 2026. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) were used for dichotomous outcomes and weighted mean differences (WMDs) for continuous outcomes. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistic. Results Twenty studies were included. In the primary pre-pandemic comparison, mortality was significantly higher during the COVID-19 era across 18 studies including 35,639 patients (OR = 1.49, 95%CI 1.20-1.85; I2 = 44.7%). Postoperative complications were also increased across 13 studies including 12,174 patients (OR = 1.44, 95%CI 1.04-1.98; I2 = 78.5%). No significant difference was observed for requirement of mechanical ventilation (OR = 1.20, 95%CI 0.81-1.76; I2 = 0.0%), whereas length-of-stay findings were inconclusive because of high heterogeneity (WMD = -1.46 days, 95%CI -3.19 to 0.28; I2 = 85.8%). Conclusions Neurosurgical patients managed during the COVID-19 era had higher mortality and postoperative complication rates than those treated before the pandemic. These findings highlight the vulnerability of neurosurgical care systems to large-scale health-system disruption and underscore the need for resilient strategies to ensure timely and safer neurosurgical care during future disruptions. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): Nanoscopy reveals heparan sulfate clusters as docking sites for SARS-CoV-2 attachment and entry
abstract: Abstract Virus entry is thought to involve binding a unique receptor for cell attachment and cytosolic entry. For SARS-CoV-2 underlying the COVID-19 pandemic, angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) is widely considered the receptor for cell-surface attachment and cytosolic entry. Using advanced light microscopy to resolve individual virions and receptors, we found instead that heparan sulfate (HS), not ACE2, mediates SARS-CoV-2 cell-surface attachment and subsequent endocytosis. ACE2 functions only downstream of HS to enable viral genome expression. Instead of binding single HS molecules that electrostatically interact with viral surface proteins weakly, SARS-CoV-2 binds clusters of ∼6–137 HS molecules projecting 60–410 nm above the plasma membrane. These tall, HS-rich clusters, present at about one per 6 μm2, act as docking sites for viral attachment. Blocking HS binding with the clinically used HS-binding agent pixantrone strongly inhibited an authentic pathogen, the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron JN.1 subvariant, from attaching to and infecting human airway cells. This work establishes a revised entry paradigm in which HS clusters mediate SARS-CoV-2 attachment and endocytosis, with ACE2 acting downstream, thereby identifying HS interactions as a key anti-COVID-19 strategy. This paradigm and its therapeutic implications may apply broadly beyond COVID-19 because, analogous to SARS-CoV-2, HS binds many other viruses but is only considered an attachment regulator. Statement of Significance Viral entry, a crucial antiviral target, is typically thought to involve binding its unique receptor for the cell surface attachment and subsequent entry. We examined this concept with advanced microscopies to resolve individual receptors and SARS-CoV-2 virions responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. We discovered two receptors for viral entry: heparan sulfate, a polysaccharide that may bind many viruses, mediates viral attachment and subsequent endocytosis, whereas angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), the generally assumed SARS-CoV-2 receptor, acts only downstream to facilitate viral infection. This model suggests perturbation of HS binding as a more effective anti-COVID-19 strategy than previously recognized. It may apply broadly beyond COVID-19 because, analogous to SARS-CoV-2, HS binds many other viruses but is only considered an attachment regulator.

title: Ethnic reporting and representation in UK COVID-19 consenting observational studies; a systematic review
abstract: Background Evidence suggests ethnic minority populations are disproportionately impacted by COVID-19, however ethnic minority groups are often under-represented in research with ethnicity associations not being investigated. Observational studies are an important tool for understanding the health inequalities of ethnic minority populations. We aimed to assess the reporting of ethnic composition and representation of ethnic minority groups in COVID-19 consented observational studies in the UK. Methods A systematic review of COVID-19 studies was conducted in OVID MedLine electronic database (1 st January 2020-22 nd November 2022). Observational, opt-in consenting studies of COVID-19 exposures and outcomes with a minimum of 96 participants in the UK only were eligible. Studies that were non-medical, COVID-19 vaccination studies and studies investigating the impact of COVID-19 policies were excluded as were studies that registered only children (<18 years). Data analysis was conducted in R v4.3.3. Results This systematic review comprised of 138 studies of which 100 (72.5%) reported participant ethnicity, most commonly through self-reporting by participants. Only 15 of the studies reporting ethnicity (15%) used the recognised ONS ethnicity categories for reporting participant ethnicity. Studies acquired their data either through self-conducted studies or from large, observational study databases. UK-Biobank data was the most common database being used for 69 (50%) of the studies. Conclusion Reporting of participant ethnicity in consenting, observational COVID-19 studies in the UK was found to be inconsistent or missing despite early evidence of ethnic minority groups being disproportionately affected by the disease and most studies having access to, at a minimum, ONS five high-level ethnicity data through their use of large databases such as UK-Biobank. This made quantitative assessment of representation challenging. However, many studies under-represented ethnic minority participants compared to the 2021 England and Wales Census data.

title: Effects of State Medicaid Expansions Affecting Parental Eligibility on Children's Healthcare Access and Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
abstract: Objective To examine whether pre-pandemic state Medicaid expansions for adults affected children's healthcare access and utilization, child health, and parental health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods The sample includes children from households with incomes up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level using data from the 2016-2023 National Survey of Children's Health. Child outcomes include insurance coverage, usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, unmet healthcare needs, past 12-month utilization of any medical services, preventive medical and dental visits, mental health professional treatments, non-mental health specialist visits, emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and general/oral health ratings. Parent outcomes include physical and mental health ratings. Difference-in-differences models estimate year-by-year differences in outcomes between Medicaid expansion and non-expansion states. Results There is a decline in usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, and preventive medical visits in the first or second pandemic year and in child health in 2020/2023 in expansion versus non-expansion states. In contrast, there is an increase in mental health professional treatments and other specialist visits in 2021-2023 in expansion states. Lastly, there are declines in maternal physical/mental health and father's mental health in 2020 but increase in father's mental/physical health in 2023 in expansion states. Conclusion During the pandemic, children in low-income households had less care continuity and preventive care but more mental health treatments and non-mental specialist visits in Medicaid expansion versus non-expansion states. There were also declines in both child and parent health. Findings potentially reflect intertwined effects from greater parental coverage but more pandemic-related social mobility restrictions disrupting routine/preventive care and worsening mental health more in expansion states.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the effects of pre-pandemic state Medicaid expansions on children's healthcare access and health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using data from the National Survey of Children's Health, it finds that Medicaid expansion states experienced declines in routine care and preventive services but increases in mental health treatments and specialist visits. The results suggest a complex interplay between expanded parental coverage and pandemic-related disruptions. The study's findings have implications for understanding how healthcare policies affect vulnerable populations during public health crises. However, the reliance on observational data and potential confounding factors limits the strength of causal conclusions.

Lastly, there are declines in maternal physical/mental health and father's mental health in 2020 but increase in father's mental/physical health in 2023 in expansion states. title: Comparative Analysis of Nucleocapsid- and Spike-Specific Isotype Humoral Immune Responses Following Natural SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Vaccination with Sinopharm, Sinovac, and AstraZeneca.
abstract: The diversity of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) vaccine platforms and widespread natural exposure have created a complex landscape of humoral immunity requiring detailed characterization. Here, we compare nucleocapsid (N)- and spike (S)-specific antibody responses in sera from infected humans (IH) during the first pandemic wave (April–August 2020) and in vaccine recipients (Sinopharm, Sinovac, or AstraZeneca) using commercial ELISA kits. Among naturally IH, the IgG-positivity rate was higher for N (80.9%) than S (42.8%), with significantly elevated N-specific IgG levels compared to prepandemic controls ( p -value <0.05), while IgM responses showed no significant differences. Strong positive correlations were observed between S- and N-specific antibody responses, particularly for IgG and its subclasses. Vaccinated cohorts exhibited high IgG positivity rate (83–100%) against both antigens with low IgM levels, and overall IgG and subclass responses were significantly elevated relative to pre-pandemic controls ( p -value <0.05), with consistently strong inter-antigen correlations across groups. Overall, natural infection induces a coordinated humoral response biased toward the nucleocapsid antigen, supporting its utility as a marker of recent infection, whereas vaccination elicits a robust multi-subclass antibody response with platform-dependent differences in antigen recognition and subclass distribution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) and spike (S) antigens following natural infection and vaccination with different platforms, as the diversity of vaccine platforms and natural exposure has created a complex landscape of immunity requiring detailed understanding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared N- and S-specific antibody responses in sera from individuals with natural SARS-CoV-2 infection during the first pandemic wave (April–August 2020) and in vaccine recipients who had been vaccinated with Sinopharm, Sinovac, or AstraZeneca.
analysis.methods: Antibody responses were measured using commercial ELISA kits to assess IgG and IgM positivity rates against N and S antigens in sera from infected humans and vaccine recipients.
analysis.main_results: Among naturally infected individuals, the IgG-positivity rate was higher for N (80.9%) than S (42.8%), with significantly elevated N-specific IgG levels compared to prepandemic controls (p-value <0.05). Vaccinated cohorts showed high IgG positivity rates (83–100%) against both antigens with low IgM levels, and overall IgG and subclass responses were significantly elevated relative to pre-pandemic controls (p-value <0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that natural infection induces a coordinated humoral response biased toward the nucleocapsid antigen, whereas vaccination elicits a robust multi-subclass antibody response with platform-dependent differences in antigen recognition and subclass distribution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support the use of nucleocapsid-specific antibodies as a marker for recent SARS-CoV-2 infection and highlight the importance of understanding platform-dependent differences in vaccine-induced immune responses for improved surveillance and vaccine development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to sera from the first pandemic wave and does not account for long-term immunity or variant-specific responses, but the evidence is strong due to the direct comparison of antibody responses using validated ELISA methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) and spike (S) antigens following natural infection and vaccination with Sinopharm, Sinovac, and AstraZeneca. It finds that natural infection leads to higher N-specific IgG levels compared to S-specific responses, while vaccination results in robust IgG positivity against both antigens. The study highlights platform-dependent differences in vaccine-induced antibody responses and suggests the potential utility of N-specific antibodies as a marker for recent infection. The findings are supported by commercial ELISA assays and are relevant for understanding immunity dynamics. However, the study is limited to the first pandemic wave and does not address long-term immunity or variant-specific responses, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在表征自然感染后的体液 免疫应答 至 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳 (N) 和刺突 (S) 抗原以及不同平台的 疫苗接种,因为 疫苗 平台和自然暴露的多样性创造了复杂的免疫景观,需要详细了解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了第一波大流行期间(2020 年 4 月至 8 月)自然 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染者的血清中的 N 和 S 特异性抗体反应,以及接种了国药集团、科兴或阿斯利康疫苗的 疫苗 接受者的血清中的 N 和 S 特异性抗体反应。
elements_zh.methods: 使用商业 ELISA 试剂盒测量抗体反应,以评估感染者和 疫苗 受体血清中 N 和 S 抗原的 IgG 和 IgM 阳性率。
elements_zh.main_results: 在自然感染个体中,N 的 IgG 阳性率 (80.9%) 高于 S (42.8%),与大流行前对照相比,N 特异性 IgG 水平显着升高(p 值 <0.05)。接种疫苗的 队列研究 对两种低 IgM 水平的抗原表现出高 IgG 阳性率 (83-100%),并且总体 IgG 和亚类反应相对于大流行前对照显着升高(p 值 <0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,自然感染会诱导偏向核衣壳抗原的协调体液反应,而 疫苗接种 则会引发强大的多亚类抗体反应,在抗原识别和亚类分布方面具有平台依赖性差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持使用核衣壳特异性抗体作为最近 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的标记,并强调了解 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 中平台依赖性差异对于改进 监测 和 疫苗 发育的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于第一波大流行的血清,并未考虑长期免疫或变异特异性反应,但由于使用经过验证的 ELISA 方法直接比较抗体反应,因此证据充足。

analysis_zh.methods: 使用商业 ELISA 试剂盒测量抗体反应,以评估感染者和 疫苗 受体血清中 N 和 S 抗原的 IgG 和 IgM 阳性率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在自然感染个体中,N 的 IgG 阳性率 (80.9%) 高于 S (42.8%),与大流行前对照相比,N 特异性 IgG 水平显着升高(p 值 <0.05)。接种疫苗的 队列研究 对两种低 IgM 水平的抗原表现出高 IgG 阳性率 (83-100%),并且总体 IgG 和亚类反应相对于大流行前对照显着升高(p 值 <0.05)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,自然感染会诱导偏向核衣壳抗原的协调体液反应,而 疫苗接种 则会引发强大的多亚类抗体反应,在抗原识别和亚类分布方面具有平台依赖性差异。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持使用核衣壳特异性抗体作为最近 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的标记,并强调了解 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 中平台依赖性差异对于改进 监测 和 疫苗 发育的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于第一波大流行的血清,并未考虑长期免疫或变异特异性反应,但由于使用经过验证的 ELISA 方法直接比较抗体反应,因此证据充足。

title: A single Omicron mutation reshapes ORF3a-driven host-cell remodelling
abstract: ABSTRACT SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a remodels host membranes, but the structural basis and metabolic consequences of this process remain unclear. Here, we combine complementary imaging approaches to define ORF3a function at nanometric scale, identifying underlying mechanisms, and determining how Omicron variant rewire this activity. ORF3a from the ancestral Wuhan strain disrupts Golgi cisternae, drives the formation of ORF3a dense vesicles, remodels mitochondrial architecture, and promotes lipid droplet expansion. Multi-omics analyses further reveal selective triacylglycerol accumulation linked to DGAT1 upregulation, which we validate pharmacologically through DGAT1 inhibition. In contrast, Omicron ORF3a variant, despite carrying only the Thr223Ile substitution within the β7-β8 loop at the bottom of the ‘cytosolic domain’, induced a dramatic phenotypic shift: ORF3a localizes to multivesicular bodies, preserves Golgi architecture, and fails to induce lipid accumulation. All together, these results identify ORF3a as a regulator of membrane organization and lipid homeostasis, showing how minimal sequence variation rewires host-cell remodelling.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究结合了互补成像方法,在纳米尺度上定义了 ORF3a 功能,确定了潜在机制,并确定了 Omicron 变体如何重新连接该活性。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 宿主 细胞重塑 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的机制的见解,这可以为未来病毒 发病机制 的研究和靶向治疗策略的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些发现得到了多组学和药理学验证的支持,提供了中等程度的置信度。

title: Supplementation of αKG along with TGFβ/HIF1α antagonist rescues lung fibrosis in mice with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are the clinical challenges among patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), affecting ~ 10% of the survivors worldwide. PASC manifestations include pulmonary fibrosis, impaired respiratory function, and long-term morbidity. Recent WHO reports from 83 countries also describe severe morbidity among COVID-19 survivors associated with PASC, indicating an unmet need to address the issue. We developed a mouse model showing the above disease pathophysiology, and investigated the related signalling molecules, with a focus on developing targeted treatment strategies against it. METHODS: We developed the mild and severe SARS-CoV-2 infection mice models. We took the opportunity to transiently express high/low levels of hACE2 in the airways and lungs of the mice, to manipulate infection severity and longer survivability. The severe infection model developed ARDS pathogenesis and pulmonary fibrosis, limiting respiratory functions (assessed by dual-chamber plethysmography), and survived beyond 30 DPI. The signalling molecules of these pathogenic pathways were identified from related tissue/blood samples of the mice using mass spectrometry-based proteome analysis, histopathology, immunoblotting and flow cytometry. RESULTS: The proteomic analysis revealed key pathways driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and pulmonary fibrosis in mice lungs. Elevated expression of P-AKT, TGFβ and HIF1α supported the severity of ARDS and fibrosis in lungs at 15 as well as 30 DPI. We developed a treatment strategy by targeting the above signalling molecules. Treatment with dietary alpha-ketoglutarate (1% αKG daily), known suppressor of P-AKT, along with inhibitor to TGFβ (SB431542,10 mg/kg BW) or HIF1α (CAY10585, 10 mg/kg BW/daily, delivered intraperitoneally) till 7 DPI, significantly reduced EMT and fibrosis by suppressing the PAKT: TGFβ:HIF1α signalling, and finally improved mice survivability (50%) beyond 50 DPI with a restored pulmonary function. CONCLUSION: The study thus demonstrated the upregulation signalling molecules like P-AKT, TGFβ and HIF1α and their association with pulmonary fibrosis in mice after severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. Further, the inhibition of the above pathophysiology by the co-administration of αKG along with HIF1α/TGFβ antagonist highlighted a targeted therapeutic strategy against it. Importantly, for the first time, our study described the HIF1α axis as the therapeutic target in rescuing post-acute sequelae such as ARDS and fibrosis in mice with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the clinical challenges of pulmonary fibrosis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), which affect ~10% of survivors. A mouse model of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection was developed to investigate the pathophysiology and potential treatment strategies. The methods included proteomic analysis, histopathology, immunoblotting, and flow cytometry to identify key signalling molecules involved in the disease. The results showed that the severe infection model developed ARDS and pulmonary fibrosis, with elevated expression of P-AKT, TGFβ, and HIF1α. The study demonstrated that targeting these molecules with αKG and antagonists could reduce EMT and fibrosis, improving mice survivability beyond 50 DPI. The findings suggest that targeting the P-AKT, TGFβ, and HIF1α pathways may offer a therapeutic strategy for post-acute sequelae of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. The evidence is based on a mouse model and does not include limitations or evidence strength assessments.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: Pulmonary fibrosis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are the clinical challenges among patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), affecting ~ 10% of the survivors worldwide. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们开发了轻度和重度 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染小鼠模型。我们开发了显示上述疾病病理生理学的小鼠模型,并研究了相关的信号分子,重点是开发针对它的靶向 治疗 策略。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基于质谱的蛋白质组分析、组织病理学、免疫印迹和流式细胞术从小鼠的相关组织/血液样本中鉴定出这些致病途径的信号分子。我们借此机会在小鼠气道和肺部短暂表达高/低水平的 hACE2,以控制感染的严重程度和更长的生存期。

title_zh: 补充 αKG 与 TGFβ/HIF1α 拮抗剂可挽救严重 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染小鼠的肺纤维化
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are the clinical challenges among patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), affecting ~ 10% of the survivors worldwide. PASC manifestations include pulmonary fibrosis, impaired respiratory function, and long-term morbidity. Recent WHO reports from 83 countries also describe severe morbidity among COVID-19 survivors associated with PASC, indicating an unmet need to address the issue. We developed a mouse model showing the above disease pathophysiology, and investigated the related signalling molecules, with a focus on developing targeted treatment strategies against it. METHODS: We developed the mild and severe SARS-CoV-2 infection mice models. We took the opportunity to transiently express high/low levels of hACE2 in the airways and lungs of the mice, to manipulate infection severity and longer survivability. The severe infection model developed ARDS pathogenesis and pulmonary fibrosis, limiting respiratory functions (assessed by dual-chamber plethysmography), and survived beyond 30 DPI. The signalling molecules of these pathogenic pathways were identified from related tissue/blood samples of the mice using mass spectrometry-based proteome analysis, histopathology, immunoblotting and flow cytometry. RESULTS: The proteomic analysis revealed key pathways driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and pulmonary fibrosis in mice lungs. Elevated expression of P-AKT, TGFβ and HIF1α supported the severity of ARDS and fibrosis in lungs at 15 as well as 30 DPI. We developed a treatment strategy by targeting the above signalling molecules. Treatment with dietary alpha-ketoglutarate (1% αKG daily), known suppressor of P-AKT, along with inhibitor to TGFβ (SB431542,10 mg/kg BW) or HIF1α (CAY10585, 10 mg/kg BW/daily, delivered intraperitoneally) till 7 DPI, significantly reduced EMT and fibrosis by suppressing the PAKT: TGFβ:HIF1α signalling, and finally improved mice survivability (50%) beyond 50 DPI with a restored pulmonary function. CONCLUSION: The study thus demonstrated the upregulation signalling molecules like P-AKT, TGFβ and HIF1α and their association with pulmonary fibrosis in mice after severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. Further, the inhibition of the above pathophysiology by the co-administration of αKG along with HIF1α/TGFβ antagonist highlighted a targeted therapeutic strategy against it. Importantly, for the first time, our study described the HIF1α axis as the therapeutic target in rescuing post-acute sequelae such as ARDS and fibrosis in mice with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: The SARS-CoV-2 S2′-helix compared to stem-helix confers higher genetic barrier to antibody resistance
abstract: Understanding the potential for resistance to antibodies targeting conserved epitopes on the coronavirus spike protein is essential for developing broad-spectrum antivirals. The S2′-helix and stem helix represent two key conserved epitopes across multiple coronaviruses, with the S2′-helix being broadly conserved throughout the coronavirus subfamily and the stem helix primarily conserved among betacoronaviruses. Here, we demonstrate that the S2′-helix in SARS-CoV-2 possesses a higher genetic barrier to antibody resistance than the stem helix. Potent escape mutations in the stem helix, including D1153G, Y1155S, F1156L and F1156V, were selected under antibody pressure, and variants such as S1147L, E1151D, D1153G, D1153H, D1153Y and Y1155H were frequently identified in naturally circulating strains. These mutations completely abolished neutralization by some stem helix-targeting antibodies. In contrast, under pressure from S2′-helix-targeting antibodies, we did not detect clear viral escape. Only one naturally occurring mutation in the S2′-helix, L822F, was observed at considerable frequency, it weakly or mildly reduced but did not abolish neutralizing activity. Furthermore, combination therapy with S2′-helix-targeting antibodies synergistically suppressed the emergence of escape mutants selected by stem helix-directed antibodies. Our findings underscore the S2′-helix as a promising target for the design of broadly protective coronavirus therapeutics with a reduced risk of viral escape.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Understanding the potential for resistance to antibodies targeting conserved epitopes on the coronavirus spike protein is essential for developing broad-spectrum antivirals. The study aimed to compare the genetic barrier to antibody resistance between two conserved epitopes on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the genetic barrier to antibody resistance in two conserved epitopes of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein: the S2′-helix and the stem helix. It highlights that the stem helix is more susceptible to escape mutations under antibody pressure, with several mutations identified in naturally circulating strains that completely abolish neutralization by some antibodies. In contrast, the S2′-helix shows a higher genetic barrier, with only one mutation, L822F, observed at considerable frequency, which weakly or mildly reduces neutralizing activity. The findings suggest that the S2′-helix could be a more promising target for developing broadly protective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2, as it is less prone to viral escape. The study is based on abstract-only evidence, and no limitations or evidence strength are explicitly reported.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 了解针对冠状病毒 刺突蛋白 保守表位的抗体的耐药潜力对于开发广谱 刺突蛋白 至关重要。该研究旨在比较 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 上两个保守表位之间的抗体抗性遗传障碍。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体进行,重点关注自然循环菌株并检查 突变 的 S2' 螺旋和茎螺旋。该研究涉及分析抗体压力下的逃逸 突变 及其在循环变异中的频率。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及在抗体压力下选择茎螺旋中有效的逃逸突变,并鉴定自然循环菌株中经常出现的突变。它还包括评估这些 突变 针对针对 S2'-螺旋和茎螺旋的抗体的中和活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在抗体压力下选择了茎螺旋中的有效逃逸突变,包括D1153G、Y1155S、F1156L和F1156V,并且在自然循环菌株中经常鉴定出诸如S1147L、E1151D、D1153G、D1153H、D1153Y和Y1155H等变体。在 S2'-螺旋中仅观察到一种天然存在的 突变,L822F,其频率相当高,它微弱或轻微地降低但没有消除中和活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些 突变 完全消除了一些茎螺旋靶向抗体的中和作用。相比之下,在 S2' 螺旋靶向抗体的压力下,我们没有检测到明显的病毒逃逸。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 我们的研究结果强调,S2'-螺旋是设计具有广泛保护性的冠状病毒疗法的有前景的靶标,可降低病毒逃逸的风险。

title_zh: 与茎螺旋相比,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 S2′螺旋赋予抗体抗性更高的遗传屏障
source_body_en: Understanding the potential for resistance to antibodies targeting conserved epitopes on the coronavirus spike protein is essential for developing broad-spectrum antivirals. The S2′-helix and stem helix represent two key conserved epitopes across multiple coronaviruses, with the S2′-helix being broadly conserved throughout the coronavirus subfamily and the stem helix primarily conserved among betacoronaviruses. Here, we demonstrate that the S2′-helix in SARS-CoV-2 possesses a higher genetic barrier to antibody resistance than the stem helix. Potent escape mutations in the stem helix, including D1153G, Y1155S, F1156L and F1156V, were selected under antibody pressure, and variants such as S1147L, E1151D, D1153G, D1153H, D1153Y and Y1155H were frequently identified in naturally circulating strains. These mutations completely abolished neutralization by some stem helix-targeting antibodies. In contrast, under pressure from S2′-helix-targeting antibodies, we did not detect clear viral escape. Only one naturally occurring mutation in the S2′-helix, L822F, was observed at considerable frequency, it weakly or mildly reduced but did not abolish neutralizing activity. Furthermore, combination therapy with S2′-helix-targeting antibodies synergistically suppressed the emergence of escape mutants selected by stem helix-directed antibodies. Our findings underscore the S2′-helix as a promising target for the design of broadly protective coronavirus therapeutics with a reduced risk of viral escape.

title: Directed evolution of a stem-helix-targeting antibody enables MERS-CoV cross-neutralization through enhanced binding affinity.
abstract: Abstract Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) targeting conserved regions of the betacoronavirus spike are important for pan-betacoronavirus protection and pandemic preparedness. Here, we report on the isolation of a human monoclonal antibody, CC65.1, from a SARS-CoV-2 convalescent donor that targets the conserved S2 stem helix region. CC65.1 neutralizes various sarbecoviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, and binds the MERS-CoV spike but lacks MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity due to insufficient binding affinity. We utilized directed evolution to enhance the binding affinity of CC65.1 for the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, yielding engineered antibody variants with newly acquired MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity. High-resolution structural analysis reveals key paratope mutations that optimize binding and stabilize epitope engagement. Our findings demonstrate the potential of rational antibody engineering to expand bnAb breadth across divergent betacoronaviruses. This work supports the development of engineered bnAbs and S2-targeted vaccines for broad betacoronavirus countermeasures and highlights strategies to achieve cross-lineage immunity for future pandemic threats. Author Summary The persistent emergence of new SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern that evade neutralizing antibody responses and other zoonotic betacoronaviruses with pandemic potential have provided strong motivation to develop broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) that target more conserved regions of the spike protein in sarbecoviruses and other betacoronaviruses. Here, we employed a directed evolution strategy to engineer the sarbecovirus-neutralizing antibody CC65.1, which targets the conserved S2 stem helix, to enhance its binding affinity with the MERS-CoV stem helix region, thereby conferring MERS-CoV neutralization. High-resolution structural studies of engineered CC65.1 revealed that key mutations reshape the paratope to better accommodate and stabilize the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, resulting in increased binding affinity and neutralization potency. This study emphasizes the critical role of affinity maturation in expanding neutralization breadth and provides valuable insights for design of bnAbs to prevent and treat pandemic threats by betacoronaviruses.

title_zh: 茎螺旋靶向抗体的定向 进化 通过增强的结合亲和力实现 MERS-CoV 交叉中和。
source_body_en: Abstract Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) targeting conserved regions of the betacoronavirus spike are important for pan-betacoronavirus protection and pandemic preparedness. Here, we report on the isolation of a human monoclonal antibody, CC65.1, from a SARS-CoV-2 convalescent donor that targets the conserved S2 stem helix region. CC65.1 neutralizes various sarbecoviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, and binds the MERS-CoV spike but lacks MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity due to insufficient binding affinity. We utilized directed evolution to enhance the binding affinity of CC65.1 for the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, yielding engineered antibody variants with newly acquired MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity. High-resolution structural analysis reveals key paratope mutations that optimize binding and stabilize epitope engagement. Our findings demonstrate the potential of rational antibody engineering to expand bnAb breadth across divergent betacoronaviruses. This work supports the development of engineered bnAbs and S2-targeted vaccines for broad betacoronavirus countermeasures and highlights strategies to achieve cross-lineage immunity for future pandemic threats. Author Summary The persistent emergence of new SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern that evade neutralizing antibody responses and other zoonotic betacoronaviruses with pandemic potential have provided strong motivation to develop broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) that target more conserved regions of the spike protein in sarbecoviruses and other betacoronaviruses. Here, we employed a directed evolution strategy to engineer the sarbecovirus-neutralizing antibody CC65.1, which targets the conserved S2 stem helix, to enhance its binding affinity with the MERS-CoV stem helix region, thereby conferring MERS-CoV neutralization. High-resolution structural studies of engineered CC65.1 revealed that key mutations reshape the paratope to better accommodate and stabilize the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, resulting in increased binding affinity and neutralization potency. This study emphasizes the critical role of affinity maturation in expanding neutralization breadth and provides valuable insights for design of bnAbs to prevent and treat pandemic threats by betacoronaviruses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 针对 β 冠状病毒刺突保守区域的广泛中和抗体 (bnAb) 对于泛 β 冠状病毒保护和大流行防范非常重要。在这里,我们报告了从 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 恢复期供体中分离出的人单克隆抗体 CC65.1,该抗体靶向保守的 S2 茎螺旋区域。CC65.1 中和各种 sarbecovirus,包括 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,并结合 MERS-CoV 刺突,但由于结合亲和力不足,缺乏 MERS-CoV 中和活性。我们利用定向 进化 来增强 CC65.1 与 MERS-CoV S2 茎螺旋的结合亲和力,产生具有新获得的 MERS-CoV 中和活性的工程化抗体变体。高分辨率结构分析揭示了关键互补位 突变,可优化结合并稳定表位结合。我们的研究结果表明,合理的抗体工程具有扩大 bnAb 跨不同 β 冠状病毒的广度的潜力。这项工作支持开发工程化 bnAb 和 S2 靶向 疫苗,用于广泛的 β 冠状病毒对策,并强调了针对未来大流行威胁实现跨谱系免疫的策略。作者摘要 不断出现的新的 刺突蛋白 变体可以逃避中和抗体反应,以及其他具有大流行潜力的人畜共患 β 冠状病毒,这为开发针对 sarbeco 病毒和其他 β 冠状病毒中 刺突蛋白 更保守区域的广泛中和抗体 (bnAb) 提供了强大的动力。在这里,我们采用定向 进化 策略来设计 sarbecovirus 中和抗体 CC65.1,该抗体针对保守的 S2 茎螺旋,以增强其与 MERS-CoV 茎螺旋区域的结合亲和力,从而实现 MERS-CoV 中和。对工程化 CC65.1 的高分辨率结构研究表明,关键的 突变 重塑了互补位,以更好地适应和稳定 MERS-CoV S2 茎螺旋,从而提高结合亲和力和中和效力。这项研究强调了亲和力成熟在扩大中和广度方面的关键作用,并为设计 bnAb 以预防和治疗 β 冠状病毒的大流行威胁提供了宝贵的见解。

title: Clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized for COVID-19 in the periods of non-Omicron and Omicron variant dominance.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omicron is known for its higher transmissibility and milder respiratory symptoms than those of other SARS-CoV-2 variants. How comorbidities contribute to mortality outcomes in Omicron-related COVID-19 remains unclear. This study compared clinical features and outcomes between Omicron and non-Omicron variants and identified risk factors for in-hospital mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted from April 2020 to September 2022. Patients with COVID-19 infection were divided into Omicron and non-Omicron groups. Demographic data, laboratory results, and treatment information were collected and analyzed. Clinical outcomes for different variants were analyzed. RESULTS: The Omicron group had a greater burden of comorbidities but exhibited lower COVID-19 disease severity and fewer complications than did the non-Omicron group. Overall mortality was relatively high in the Omicron group, primarily due to non-COVID-related causes. In multivariate analysis, a Charlson comorbidity index score of ≥3 (odds ratio [OR] = 4.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.94-10.91, p < 0.001), severe or critical COVID-19 (OR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.24-2.07, p < 0.001), a high white blood cell count (OR = 1.00, 95% CI = 1.00-1.00, p = 0.021), and a high C-reactive protein level (OR = 1.01, 95% CI = 1.00-1.01, p = 0.003) emerged as positive predictors of COVID-19-related mortality. CONCLUSION: Severe or critical COVID-19 and a Charlson comorbidity index score of ≥3 were independently associated with high in-hospital mortality. Intensive monitoring and early intervention should be prioritized for high-risk groups to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Triggered by Mixed Plasmodium spp. and SARS-CoV-2 Coinfection
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may be triggered by infectious diseases, including malaria and viral infections. A case of mixed Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum infection concomitant with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in a patient who developed secondary HLH is described in the present study. Malaria was acquired in the endemic state of Mato Grosso, Brazil, but diagnosed in Macaé, Rio de Janeiro, a nonendemic region. The patient presented with high fever, pancytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperferritinemia. Bone marrow aspirate revealed hemophagocytosis. The patient met six of the eight HLH-2004 criteria and had an HScore indicating a high probability of secondary HLH. Recovery was achieved after the initiation of antimalarial and corticosteroid therapies. This case suggests that parasitic and viral infections may synergistically trigger immunologic “second hits,” promoting macrophage hyperactivation. Recognition of overlapping infections, particularly outside endemic areas, may facilitate earlier diagnosis and timely management of secondary HLH.

title: Long-term angiogenic and thromboinflammatory signatures in post-COVID-19 syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-COVID-19 syndrome is a major long-term sequela of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection, potentially involving persistent angiogenic and thromboinflammatory dysfunction, though long-term biomarker behavior remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the evolution of angiogenic and thromboinflammatory biomarkers in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients. METHODS: This ambispective cohort study was conducted at the National Institute of Respiratory Diseases in Mexico City. Thirty-two adults hospitalized for severe or critical COVID-19 in 2020 were followed for three and a half years. Paired plasma samples were collected during hospitalization and at long-term follow-up. Endothelial dysfunction markers included soluble P-selectin, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2, vascular endothelial growth factor D, and angiopoietin-1. Hemostasis was assessed by prothrombin time. Acute-phase proteins alpha-2-macroglobulin and haptoglobin were measured via immunoassay. Persistent symptoms were documented at follow-up. RESULTS: At three and a half years, persistent symptoms were common: fatigue in sixty-five point 6%, dyspnea in sixty-two point 5%, and concentration difficulties in sixty-five point 6%. Vascular endothelial growth factor D and angiopoietin-1 remained elevated. Alpha-2-macroglobulin stayed high, and prothrombin time was prolonged in a subset of patients. CONCLUSIONS: Severe COVID-19 survivors show sustained angiogenic dysregulation and thromboinflammatory imbalance. Elevated vascular endothelial growth factor D and angiopoietin-1 indicate ongoing angiogenic perturbations, while increased alpha-2-macroglobulin and prolonged prothrombin time reflect persistent coagulation disturbances. These biomarkers may help identify long-term vascular alterations in post-COVID-19 syndrome.

title: Workplace Violence Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Occupational Disparities in Nonfatal Violent Victimization.
abstract: This study sought to understand the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on nonfatal workplace violence (WPV) experiences of workers in different occupational groups in the United States. The 2017 to 2022 National Crime Victimization Survey data were used to generate national nonfatal WPV rates in the United States for seven occupational groups. We used a quantitative approach to compare the WPV rates across occupational groups before and during the pandemic in light of changes in the routine activities of the U.S. First, average annual WPV rates by occupational group were compared across study years to identify temporal patterns. Second, average WPV rates for the three pre-pandemic years (2017-2019) and the three pandemic years (2020-2022) were compared to assess changes associated with the pandemic. Third, paired samples t -tests were conducted to determine whether differences in WPV rates between the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods were statistically significant for each occupational group. Our analysis of overall patterns revealed several temporal shifts: WPV rates sharply declined in the first pandemic year, surged in the second year, and shifted downward again in the third year. We also found that WPV rates varied across occupational groups and pandemic years, suggesting that these trends reflect differential changes in working environments across occupational groups during distinct phases of the pandemic. These findings highlight the complex and heterogenous impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on WPV and underscore the importance of considering occupational and contextual differences when developing policies and interventions to mitigate WPV during public health emergencies.

analysis.scope_and_question: Workplace violence (WPV) experiences among U.S. workers across seven occupational groups during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on temporal changes in nonfatal victimization rates and occupational disparities.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review used a quantitative approach analyzing 2017–2022 National Crime Victimization Survey data to compare WPV rates across occupational groups before (2017–2019) and during (2020–2022) the pandemic using paired samples t-tests and average annual rate comparisons.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The analysis identified three distinct temporal patterns in WPV rates: a sharp decline in the first pandemic year, a surge in the second year, and a downward shift in the third year, with significant variation across occupational groups reflecting differential changes in working environments during pandemic phases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report occupational-specific risk factors, mechanisms underlying temporal shifts, or subgroup analyses (e.g., gender, race/ethnicity) that could explain heterogeneity in WPV trends across occupational groups.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings emphasize the need for occupational and contextual tailoring of WPV mitigation policies during public health emergencies, particularly to address differential impacts observed across worker groups and pandemic phases.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzed U.S. National Crime Victimization Survey data from 2017 to 2022 to assess nonfatal workplace violence (WPV) rates across seven occupational groups before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using quantitative methods, it identified three distinct temporal patterns: a sharp decline in WPV in the first pandemic year, a surge in the second year, and a downward shift in the third year. Significant variation in WPV rates across occupational groups suggested differential impacts of pandemic-related changes in working environments. The review highlights the complex and heterogeneous nature of WPV trends during the pandemic and underscores the importance of occupational and contextual considerations in developing targeted mitigation strategies.

elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report occupational-specific risk factors, mechanisms underlying temporal shifts, or subgroup analyses (e.g., gender, race/ethnicity) that could explain heterogeneity in WPV trends across occupational groups.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings emphasize the need for occupational and contextual tailoring of WPV mitigation policies during public health emergencies, particularly to address differential impacts observed across worker groups and pandemic phases.

title_zh: Workplace Violence Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Occupational Disparities in Nonfatal Violent Victimization.
source_body_en: This study sought to understand the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on nonfatal workplace violence (WPV) experiences of workers in different occupational groups in the United States. The 2017 to 2022 National Crime Victimization Survey data were used to generate national nonfatal WPV rates in the United States for seven occupational groups. We used a quantitative approach to compare the WPV rates across occupational groups before and during the pandemic in light of changes in the routine activities of the U.S. First, average annual WPV rates by occupational group were compared across study years to identify temporal patterns. Second, average WPV rates for the three pre-pandemic years (2017-2019) and the three pandemic years (2020-2022) were compared to assess changes associated with the pandemic. Third, paired samples t -tests were conducted to determine whether differences in WPV rates between the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods were statistically significant for each occupational group. Our analysis of overall patterns revealed several temporal shifts: WPV rates sharply declined in the first pandemic year, surged in the second year, and shifted downward again in the third year. We also found that WPV rates varied across occupational groups and pandemic years, suggesting that these trends reflect differential changes in working environments across occupational groups during distinct phases of the pandemic. These findings highlight the complex and heterogenous impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on WPV and underscore the importance of considering occupational and contextual differences when developing policies and interventions to mitigate WPV during public health emergencies.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity: integrating IC50 regression and activity classification using multi-task neural networks
abstract: Accurate prediction of compound bioactivity is essential for accelerating antiviral drug discovery and reducing experimental costs. Machine learning (ML) methods have shown considerable promise in modeling structure–activity relationships and compound potency. In this study, we present an integrated ML framework for predicting IC50 and pIC50 values of compounds active against SARS-CoV-2, key indicators of antiviral potency. The proposed framework comprises three complementary approaches: (i) a regression model for quantitative IC50 prediction validated against experimental data; (ii) a classification model that categorizes compounds into active and inactive classes to support compound prioritization; and (iii) a multi-task neural network that jointly performs IC50 regression and activity classification, enhancing predictive performance and interpretability. A distinctive feature of this work is the incorporation of ligand efficiency (LE) as a criterion for activity classification, offering an alternative perspective on compound prioritization that has not been previously explored in SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity modeling. The proposed models demonstrate strong predictive capability, achieving a coefficient of determination (\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$R^2$$\end{document}) of 0.77 using a neural network with feature selection, while the Random Forest classifier attains an accuracy, precision, and recall of approximately 0.92. These results highlight the potential of integrated regression, classification, and multi-task learning approaches as scalable and cost-effective tools for SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity prediction and antiviral drug discovery.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Accurate prediction of compound bioactivity is essential for accelerating antiviral drug discovery and reducing experimental costs, yet conventional methods are resource-intensive. This study addressed the knowledge gap in rapid, scalable prediction of SARS-CoV-2 antiviral potency by developing machine learning frameworks tailored to IC50 and pIC50 values.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed an integrated machine learning framework to predict SARS-CoV-2 compound bioactivity without specifying a human or animal population, datasets, or study setting. The framework was constructed using computational models rather than experimental cohorts.
analysis.methods: The proposed framework combined three approaches: a regression model for quantitative IC50 prediction validated against experimental data, a classification model to categorize compounds as active or inactive, and a multi-task neural network that jointly performed IC50 regression and activity classification. Ligand efficiency was incorporated as a criterion for activity classification.
analysis.main_results: The regression model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.77 using a neural network with feature selection, while the Random Forest classifier attained accuracy, precision, and recall of approximately 0.92. These results indicate strong predictive capability for SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the potential of integrated regression, classification, and multi-task learning approaches as scalable and cost-effective tools for SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity prediction. The novelty lies in incorporating ligand efficiency as an activity classification criterion, which had not been previously explored in SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity modeling.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that machine learning-based prediction of SARS-CoV-2 compound bioactivity could streamline antiviral drug discovery pipelines by prioritizing compounds with higher predicted potency and reducing reliance on labor-intensive experimental assays.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report external validation, generalization to diverse compound libraries, or assessment of model robustness across SARS-CoV-2 variants. The abstract-only evidence limits confidence to moderate, pending full methodological and validation details.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed an integrated machine learning framework to predict SARS-CoV-2 antiviral compound bioactivity by combining IC50 regression, activity classification, and a multi-task neural network. The regression model achieved an R2 of 0.77, while the Random Forest classifier reached approximately 0.92 in accuracy, precision, and recall. The novelty lies in incorporating ligand efficiency as a classification criterion, which had not been previously applied to SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity modeling. The authors interpret these results as demonstrating the potential of scalable, cost-effective tools to accelerate antiviral drug discovery. The findings imply that such models could prioritize compounds with higher predicted potency, reducing reliance on experimental assays. However, the abstract-only evidence limits confidence, as external validation, generalization, and robustness across variants remain unreported.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 准确预测化合物生物活性对于加速 抗病毒药物 药物发现和降低实验成本至关重要,但传统方法是资源密集型的。本研究通过开发针对 IC50 和 pIC50 值的机器学习框架,解决了快速、可扩展地预测 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗病毒药物 效力的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究设计了一个集成的机器学习框架来预测 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 化合物的生物活性,而无需指定人类或动物群体、数据集或研究设置。该框架是使用计算模型而不是实验 队列研究 构建的。
elements_zh.methods: 所提出的框架结合了三种方法:根据实验数据验证定量 IC50 预测的回归模型、将化合物分类为活性或非活性的分类模型,以及联合执行 IC50 回归和活性分类的多任务神经网络。配体效率被纳入活性分类的标准。
elements_zh.main_results: 使用具有特征选择的神经网络,回归模型的确定系数 (R2) 达到 0.77,而随机森林分类器的准确度、精确度和召回率约为 0.92。这些结果表明对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 生物活性的强大预测能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了集成回归、分类和多任务学习方法作为 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 生物活性预测的可扩展且经济有效的工具的潜力。新颖之处在于将配体效率作为活性分类标准,这在之前的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 生物活性模型中尚未探索过。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于机器学习的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 化合物生物活性预测可以通过优先考虑具有较高预测效力的化合物并减少对劳动密集型实验测定的依赖来简化 抗病毒药物 药物发现流程。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据不报告外部验证、对不同化合物库的泛化或对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的模型稳健性的评估。仅摘要的证据将信心限制在中等、悬而未决的完整方法论和验证细节上。

title: COVID-19 Vaccination Refusal Among Cancer Survivors in the United States: A Scoping Review
abstract: Cancer survivors face an elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes and were prioritized for vaccination, yet reported rates of vaccination refusal in this population vary widely. The objective of this scoping review was to map the available evidence on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among adult cancer survivors in the United States, to characterize the reported barriers and enablers, and to examine how differences in measurement account for variation in the reported estimates. PubMed, EBSCOhost, CINAHL, medRxiv, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between 1 December 2020 and 30 April 2026 reporting primary data on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among U.S. adults with a current or previous cancer diagnosis. Findings were charted and summarized descriptively. Six sources comprising 3344 participants met the eligibility criteria. Reported refusal ranged from 7.3% to 39.0%, a more than fivefold difference, with a median of 14.7%. This variation corresponded closely to what each source measured: declination of an offered vaccine, likelihood of acceptance on a Likert scale, hesitancy assessed before vaccines were widely available, or observed non-receipt of any dose. Barriers included concerns about vaccine safety, efficacy, and interaction with cancer treatment, mistrust of science and government, and low perceived need; clinician recommendation was the most consistent enabler. Estimates of vaccination refusal in this population are not directly comparable and should be interpreted alongside the construct measured.

title: Proteomic and Phosphoproteomic Characteristics of Multiple Brain Regions in Rhesus Macaques After SARS-CoV-2 Infection.
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant is more contagious than the original Alpha variant and can still cause neurological symptoms, including cognitive impairment. To gain a deeper understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying these neurological effects, this study was conducted. Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses were carried out utilizing LC-MS/MS. Samples included brainstem, cerebellum, frontal lobe, occipital lobe, parietal lobe, and temporal lobe from SARS-CoV-2 Omicron-infected and noninfected control rhesus macaques. Infection with Omicron resulted in inflammatory responses across all six brain regions, and significant regional-specific molecular alterations were observed. Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses revealed extensive abnormalities in immune activation, synaptic function, DNA repair, and signaling pathways across different brain regions. We further predicted key kinases and identified candidate proteins with significantly altered expression. This study reveals region-specific inflammatory and signaling signatures in the brain following Omicron infection. The recognized kinases and proteins with abnormal regulation serve as potential candidates for drug discovery. This can aid in formulating new therapeutic approaches for neurological issues related to COVID-19.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for neurological complications associated with COVID-19.

title: SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid induces hyperinflammation and vascular leakage through the Toll-like receptor signaling axis in macrophages.
abstract: A substantial proportion of hospitalized COVID-19 patients require ICU admission, often associated with an imbalance between antiviral responses and inflammatory signaling leading to uncontrolled cytokine secretion. The SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein is a known immune antagonist, but its role in macrophage-driven cytokine storms is unclear. We demonstrate that N functions in a stimulus-specific manner, specifically amplifying extracellular and dampening intracellular RNA sensing. Moreover, we show that this is a conserved feature of pathogenic betacoronaviruses through distinct mechanisms. Our interaction networks with SARS-CoV-2 variant N proteins suggest that the Delta variant N drives inflammation through interactions with several proteins, most notably, cGAS. Profiling of secreted cytokines revealed that N disrupts the secretome in a variant-specific manner. Most notably, we found that supernatants from the Delta variant N-expressing macrophages dramatically disrupt heart endothelial barriers, implicating N in COVID-19-associated cardiac complications. Our findings highlight N-mediated immune imbalance as a driver of severe COVID-19 and identify N as a promising therapeutic target to mitigate hyperinflammation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses why some SARS-CoV-2 infections progress to severe COVID-19 with hyperinflammation and vascular complications, noting that hospitalized patients often require ICU care due to an imbalance between antiviral responses and inflammatory signaling leading to uncontrolled cytokine secretion.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research investigates the role of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein in macrophage-driven cytokine storms, focusing on its immune-modulatory functions and variant-specific effects.
analysis.methods: The authors examined how the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein modulates extracellular and intracellular RNA sensing in macrophages, including its interactions with cGAS and effects on cytokine secretion profiles across SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.main_results: Profiling of secreted cytokines revealed variant-specific disruption of the secretome by the nucleocapsid protein, with supernatants from macrophages expressing the Delta variant N protein causing dramatic disruption of heart endothelial barriers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein as a driver of severe COVID-19 through immune imbalance, highlighting its conserved role across pathogenic betacoronaviruses and variant-specific mechanisms, including interactions with cGAS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that targeting the nucleocapsid protein could mitigate hyperinflammation in severe COVID-19 and potentially address cardiac complications associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks detailed experimental context, sample sizes, or statistical analyses, which constrains the strength of the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein as a driver of macrophage-mediated hyperinflammation and vascular leakage, a hallmark of severe COVID-19. The authors demonstrate that N amplifies extracellular RNA sensing while dampening intracellular responses, a conserved feature among pathogenic betacoronaviruses. Variant-specific analyses reveal that the Delta variant N protein disrupts cytokine secretion and disrupts heart endothelial barriers, implicating N in COVID-19-associated cardiac complications. The findings suggest N as a therapeutic target to mitigate hyperinflammation, though the evidence is confined to abstract-level data and lacks detailed experimental validation.

source_body_en: A substantial proportion of hospitalized COVID-19 patients require ICU admission, often associated with an imbalance between antiviral responses and inflammatory signaling leading to uncontrolled cytokine secretion. The SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein is a known immune antagonist, but its role in macrophage-driven cytokine storms is unclear. We demonstrate that N functions in a stimulus-specific manner, specifically amplifying extracellular and dampening intracellular RNA sensing. Moreover, we show that this is a conserved feature of pathogenic betacoronaviruses through distinct mechanisms. Our interaction networks with SARS-CoV-2 variant N proteins suggest that the Delta variant N drives inflammation through interactions with several proteins, most notably, cGAS. Profiling of secreted cytokines revealed that N disrupts the secretome in a variant-specific manner. Most notably, we found that supernatants from the Delta variant N-expressing macrophages dramatically disrupt heart endothelial barriers, implicating N in COVID-19-associated cardiac complications. Our findings highlight N-mediated immune imbalance as a driver of severe COVID-19 and identify N as a promising therapeutic target to mitigate hyperinflammation.

title: When reoxygenation fails: a dynamical model of HIF-1$$\alpha $$-mediated metabolic breakdown under hypoxia and SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Cells normally combine glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to meet energy demands, but this balance shifts under pathological conditions. During SARS-CoV-2 infection, hypoxia, viral entry, and elevated tissue lactate alter cellular metabolism. To explore these effects, we propose a parsimonious mathematical model describing how oxygen levels, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate jointly regulate metabolic balance through HIF-1 α protein, inside the cell, accounting for lactate's biphasic, non-monotonic influence on glycolysis. Model simulations reveal a single steady state whose position on the glycolysis-OXPHOS phase plane depends on environmental conditions, namely, oxygen concentration, infection, and extracellular lactate. We identify four metabolic regimes, determined by sufficiency of energy production and the driving process (OXPHOS or glycolysis). Decreasing the oxygen shifts cells from OXPHOS to glycolysis dominance in both infected and non-infected states, but infected cells may become energy-deficient even with sufficient oxygen due to virus-induced mitochondrial damage. Rising extracellular lactate initially promotes glycolysis but ultimately suppresses it at high levels, pushing cells into severe energy deficit with inhibited glycolysis. Simulations of reoxygenation exhibit hysteresis: cells pass through an energy-deficient zone during hypoxia onset but return through a safer trajectory when oxygen is restored; a vulnerability is higher in infected cells. Overall, the model clarifies metabolic trajectories during viral infection, suggesting that early hypoxia is particularly dangerous and that severe acidosis can further collapse energy production. Preventing or rapidly reversing hypoxia in respiratory infection may protect cells from energy failure and limit harmful lactate accumulation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how SARS-CoV-2 infection alters cellular metabolism under hypoxia, particularly the interplay between oxygen levels, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate in regulating metabolic balance through HIF-1α protein.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a mathematical model to simulate metabolic dynamics in cells under hypoxia and SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on the regulation of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) by HIF-1α protein.
analysis.methods: The model incorporated oxygen concentration, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate as variables to describe their joint regulation of metabolic balance, with particular attention to lactate's biphasic influence on glycolysis.
analysis.main_results: Model simulations revealed a single steady state on the glycolysis-OXPHOS phase plane, influenced by oxygen concentration, infection, and extracellular lactate. Four metabolic regimes were identified based on energy production sufficiency and the dominant process (OXPHOS or glycolysis).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that decreasing oxygen shifts cells toward glycolysis dominance, but infected cells may still face energy deficiency due to mitochondrial damage. The model highlights the dangers of early hypoxia and the potential for severe acidosis to collapse energy production.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that preventing or reversing hypoxia in respiratory infections could protect cells from energy failure and reduce harmful lactate accumulation, offering insights for therapeutic strategies in managing SARS-CoV-2-related metabolic disturbances.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mathematical model, which may not fully capture in vivo complexities. However, the model provides a clear framework for understanding metabolic shifts during SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a moderate level of confidence based on the abstract-only evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a mathematical model to explore how SARS-CoV-2 infection affects cellular metabolism under hypoxia, focusing on the role of HIF-1α protein in regulating glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). The model identifies four metabolic regimes and demonstrates that infected cells are more vulnerable to energy deficiency even with sufficient oxygen. It also highlights the biphasic effect of extracellular lactate on glycolysis and the hysteresis observed during reoxygenation. The results suggest that early hypoxia is particularly dangerous and that severe acidosis can further impair energy production. These findings have implications for understanding metabolic changes in SARS-CoV-2 infection and could inform strategies to prevent energy failure and lactate accumulation. The study's reliance on a mathematical model limits its direct applicability to real-world scenarios, but it provides a valuable framework for further research.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用数学模型模拟缺氧和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染下细胞的代谢动力学,重点研究HIF-1α蛋白对糖酵解和氧化磷酸化(OXPHOS)的调节。
elements_zh.methods: 该模型将氧浓度、病毒浸润和细胞外乳酸作为变量来描述它们对代谢平衡的联合调节,特别关注乳酸对糖酵解的双相影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 模型模拟揭示了糖酵解-OXPHOS 相平面上的单一稳态,受氧浓度、感染和细胞外乳酸的影响。根据能量产生充足性和主要过程(OXPHOS 或糖酵解)确定了四种代谢模式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,减少氧气会使细胞转向糖酵解主导地位,但受感染的细胞仍可能因线粒体损伤而面临能量不足。该模型强调了早期缺氧的危险以及严重酸中毒导致能量产生崩溃的可能性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,预防或逆转呼吸道感染中的缺氧可以保护细胞免受能量衰竭并减少有害的乳酸积累,为管理 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 相关代谢紊乱的治疗策略提供见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于数学模型,可能无法完全捕捉体内的复杂性。然而,该模型为理解 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染期间的代谢变化提供了一个清晰的框架,并且基于仅抽象的证据具有中等程度的置信度。

abstract_zh: 细胞通常结合糖酵解和氧化磷酸化(OXPHOS)来满足能量需求,但这种平衡在病理条件下会发生变化。在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染期间,缺氧、病毒进入和组织乳酸升高会改变细胞代谢。为了探索这些影响,我们提出了一个简洁的数学模型,描述氧水平、病毒浸润和细胞外乳酸如何通过细胞内的 HIF-1 α 蛋白共同调节代谢平衡,解释乳酸对糖酵解的双相、非单调影响。模型模拟揭示了单一稳态,其在糖酵解-OXPHOS 相平面上的位置取决于环境条件,即氧浓度、感染和细胞外乳酸。我们确定了四种代谢模式,由能量产生的充足性和驱动过程(OXPHOS 或糖酵解)决定。在感染和未感染状态下,氧气的减少会使细胞从 OXPHOS 转变为糖酵解主导,但由于病毒诱导的线粒体损伤,即使氧气充足,受感染的细胞也可能会变得能量不足。细胞外乳酸的增加最初会促进糖酵解,但最终会在高水平上抑制糖酵解,从而使细胞陷入严重的能量不足,糖酵解受到抑制。再氧合的模拟表现出滞后现象:细胞在缺氧开始时穿过能量缺乏区域,但在氧气恢复时通过更安全的轨迹返回;受感染细胞的脆弱性更高。总体而言,该模型阐明了病毒感染期间的代谢轨迹,表明早期缺氧特别危险,严重的酸中毒会进一步破坏能量产生。预防或快速逆转呼吸道感染中的缺氧可以保护细胞免受能量衰竭并限制有害的乳酸积累。

title: Impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the progression of Alzheimer's disease: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with neurological sequelae and may accelerate Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression through neuroinflammation and protein aggregation. However, longitudinal evidence regarding the cognitive impact of COVID-19 in patients with AD remains scarce, and this interaction requires further clarification. Objective To explore whether COVID-19 accelerates cognitive decline in patients with AD. Methods A total of 120 participants were enrolled, including 63 in the COVID-19 group and 57 in the non-COVID-19 group. The primary outcomes were disease decline and disease deterioration over three months, assessed using CDR-SB. Disease deterioration indicated clinically meaningful worsening, whereas disease decline captured subtler progression. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, lifestyle, genetic, and disease severity factors. Overlap-Weighted Propensity Score Matching was additionally performed to reduce confounding during the 3-month follow-up. Results COVID-19 significantly increased the risk of disease decline (OR = 10.39, 95% CI:3.87 to 27.87, p < 0.001) and disease deterioration (OR = 10.37, 95% CI: 2.71 to 39.65, p = 0.001). APOE ε4 carrier status was associated with a higher risk of deterioration (OR = 1.72), while those with unknown APOE status exhibited an even greater risk (OR = 5.20, 95% CI:1.32 to 20.53, p = 0.019). Secondary analyses confirmed that COVID-19 patients experienced significantly greater increases in CDR-SB scores compared to non-COVID-19 patients. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with greater short-term cognitive worsening over a three-month period in patients with AD, underscoring its potential public health relevance and the need for early surveillance to guide timely clinical management.

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染对阿尔茨海默病进展的影响:一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究。
source_body_en: Background SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with neurological sequelae and may accelerate Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression through neuroinflammation and protein aggregation. However, longitudinal evidence regarding the cognitive impact of COVID-19 in patients with AD remains scarce, and this interaction requires further clarification. Objective To explore whether COVID-19 accelerates cognitive decline in patients with AD. Methods A total of 120 participants were enrolled, including 63 in the COVID-19 group and 57 in the non-COVID-19 group. The primary outcomes were disease decline and disease deterioration over three months, assessed using CDR-SB. Disease deterioration indicated clinically meaningful worsening, whereas disease decline captured subtler progression. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, lifestyle, genetic, and disease severity factors. Overlap-Weighted Propensity Score Matching was additionally performed to reduce confounding during the 3-month follow-up. Results COVID-19 significantly increased the risk of disease decline (OR = 10.39, 95% CI:3.87 to 27.87, p < 0.001) and disease deterioration (OR = 10.37, 95% CI: 2.71 to 39.65, p = 0.001). APOE ε4 carrier status was associated with a higher risk of deterioration (OR = 1.72), while those with unknown APOE status exhibited an even greater risk (OR = 5.20, 95% CI:1.32 to 20.53, p = 0.019). Secondary analyses confirmed that COVID-19 patients experienced significantly greater increases in CDR-SB scores compared to non-COVID-19 patients. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with greater short-term cognitive worsening over a three-month period in patients with AD, underscoring its potential public health relevance and the need for early surveillance to guide timely clinical management.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染与神经系统后遗症相关,并可能通过神经炎症和蛋白质聚集加速阿尔茨海默病 (AD) 的进展。该研究旨在解决 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 对 AD 患者认知影响的知识差距。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用多变量逻辑回归来调整人口、临床、生活方式、遗传和疾病严重程度因素。进行重叠加权倾向评分匹配是为了减少 3 个月随访期间的混杂因素。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要在阿尔茨海默病(AD)患者中早期开展监测,以指导及时的临床管理并为公共卫生策略提供依据,从而应对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染。

title: Evaluation of One-Step amplicon-based targeted enrichment for SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequencing using the Midnight amplicon scheme.
abstract: Genomic surveillance proved invaluable during the COVID-19 pandemic for tracking SARS-CoV-2 variants and guiding outbreak responses, underscoring the ongoing need to reduce whole-genome sequencing (WGS) costs and improve workflow efficiency to ensure accessibility in resource limited settings. Here, we evaluated a one-step reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) approach using the Midnight V2 primer scheme for targeted amplification of the SARS-CoV-2 genome, assessed its compatibility with Illumina sequencing, and compared its performance to a well-established two-step method. Initially, we determined optimal RT-PCR reaction conditions using the Midnight V2 primer panel for the one-step RT-PCR kit and scaled reaction volumes for both RT-PCR and library preparation. Clinical specimens (n=53) that had undergone routine WGS for surveillance purposes using the established two-step RT-PCR method were compared using the one-step RT-PCR assay. For samples with genome completeness greater than 70%, both methods gave comparable results with similar sequence coverage and 100% concordance for lineage assignment. Further investigation revealed a higher percentage of reads aligning to the SARS-CoV-2 genome with a greater depth of coverage using the one-step method compared to the two-step method. Finally, analysis of scaled one-step and library reaction volumes revealed significant cost savings for samples undergoing WGS. Overall, the results presented here verify the accuracy and reproducibility of one-step targeted amplification and offer an efficient and cost-effective workflow for routine SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance.

title: Understanding the interactions and effect of environmental biofilms on SARS- CoV-2 viability on contact surfaces
abstract: Abstract Aims To investigate the role of multispecies drain biofilms in SARS-CoV-2 infectivity and persistence on contact surfaces used in meat processing plants. Methods and Results Environmental drain biofilms from pork (n = 12) and beef (n = 22) processing plants were grown with and without SARS-CoV-2 on stainless steel (S.S.), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), tile, and galvanized steel (G.S.) at 7°C for 5 days. Biofilm biomass, viral RNA persistence, and viral infectivity were quantified and compared with controls. Surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence with PVC, tile, and particularly G.S. supporting increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence relative to virus controls (p 2-fold; p < 0.01) while reducing growth of beef drain biofilms on S.S. (0.9–1.8 log reductions; p < 0.01). Conclusions Drain biofilms may act as transient reservoirs for SARS-CoV-2, with viral persistence governed by the combined effects of surface properties, biofilm structure, and microbial origin.

Methods and Results Environmental drain biofilms from pork (n = 12) and beef (n = 22) processing plants were grown with and without SARS-CoV-2 on stainless steel (S.S.), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), tile, and galvanized steel (G.S.) at 7°C for 5 days. Biofilm biomass, viral RNA persistence, and viral infectivity were quantified and compared with controls. Surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence with PVC, tile, and particularly G.S. supporting increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence relative to virus controls (p 2-fold; p < 0.01) while reducing growth of beef drain biofilms on S.S. (0.9–1.8 log reductions; p < 0.01). Conclusions Drain biofilms may act as transient reservoirs for SARS-CoV-2, with viral persistence governed by the combined effects of surface properties, biofilm structure, and microbial origin.

Biofilms from pork and beef processing facilities were grown on various materials at 7°C for 5 days with and without SARS-CoV-2. The results showed that surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence, with PVC, tile, and galvanized steel showing increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence compared to virus controls (p < 0.01).
